EP2833594.headline: Spotting network break-ins with layered AI
EP2833594.summary: Computer networks are constantly probed by attackers, and the tell-tale signs are easy to miss. Here three artificial neural networks examine incoming traffic in turn, each refining the previous one's judgement, before a final step labels suspicious activity by type of attack. The aim is more accurate and reliable detection of intrusions.

EP2849524.headline: Splitting mobile network scheduling between cell and user
EP2849524.summary: Mobile base stations must constantly decide which users get radio capacity and when. This design moves that work into shared computing, with one scheduler looking after the whole cell and separate ones for individual users, which exchange information to assign capacity and set up connections. It aims to make mobile networks more flexible and efficient.

EP2994618.headline: Keeping ice off a jet engine's airflow divider
EP2994618.summary: Inside a jet engine, a ring-shaped nose splits incoming air between the core and the bypass duct, and ice forming on it is dangerous. This design builds a hollow chamber into the nose and feeds warm air through small slots across its inner surface and out through exit openings, keeping the leading edge ice-free.

EP2881898.headline: One question, several digital assistants answer
EP2881898.summary: Digital assistants tend to specialise, so no single one knows everything. This platform keeps a register of assistants and the topics they cover, works out which are relevant to a user's question, sends the question to each of them, and then combines or selects their replies into a single response for the user.

EP3028279.headline: Storing data in tiny magnetic whirls
EP3028279.summary: Computer memory needs ever smaller and more energy-efficient ways to hold information. This device stores data using skyrmions, minute stable swirls of magnetism within a material. Different features of a group of these swirls stand for different stored values, so each element can hold more than a simple one or zero.

EP2884226.headline: Self-aligning cameras for driver-assistance systems
EP2884226.summary: Cameras fitted to cars must know exactly how they are angled relative to the vehicle, or lane-keeping and similar systems misjudge the road. While the car is moving, this method watches the painted lane markings and repeatedly refines its estimate of the camera's tilt, swivel and roll until the corrections become negligible.

EP2943894.headline: Showing only the font styling options that work
EP2943894.summary: Modern fonts can support many typographic refinements, but any given font offers only some of them. This text editor checks which features the chosen font actually provides for a selected piece of text, and then offers the user only those options, avoiding confusion over settings that would have no effect.

EP2959383.headline: A common language for connected devices
EP2959383.summary: As more everyday objects go online, devices from different makers struggle to understand one another's data. This proposes a shared way of organising information into categories such as content, context, policies, decisions and events, with links between them, so that devices and services in the internet of things can exchange information consistently.

EP2778933.headline: Faster storage after a server restart
EP2778933.summary: Storage systems speed up access by keeping frequently used data in a fast cache, but a restart usually wipes it, so performance suffers until the cache refills. This controller keeps a record of what the cache holds, plus a log of changes, and uses them after a reboot to restore the cache quickly.

EP2779462.headline: Cleaner timing signals for digital-to-analogue converters
EP2779462.summary: Chips that turn digital data into analogue signals, as in audio and radio equipment, rely on a precise timing signal, and small flaws in it degrade output quality. Here spare copies of the converter's cells measure the timing errors from the inside and feed corrections back, so the clock is adjusted exactly where it matters.

EP2779569.headline: Detecting cyber attacks on industrial plant
EP2779569.summary: Power stations and factories run on control systems that are increasingly targets for hackers. This system watches how the physical equipment is actually behaving, compares it against rules describing normal operation, and flags anomalies or intrusions, so attacks can be recognised and blocked even when they slip past conventional network defences.

EP2973290.headline: Finding the right local audience for adverts
EP2973290.summary: Advertisers want to reach people likely to be interested in a campaign. The method logs what content one group of users consumes, sorts it into topics, and links those topics to people within a particular trading area. By matching profiles to the campaign's topic, it then identifies a second group of users to target.

EP2790146.headline: Fewer wrongly blocked card payments
EP2790146.summary: Fraud checks on card transactions often decline legitimate purchases, annoying customers. This approach uses a shopper's past spending and profile to estimate how likely they are to buy from a given type of merchant, and feeds that likelihood into the real-time fraud score, so an unusual-looking but plausible purchase is less likely to be refused.

EP3865557.headline: Turning waste plastic into chemical building blocks
EP3865557.summary: Plastic waste could be a raw material for new chemicals rather than landfill. This process mixes a standard oil-refinery cracking catalyst with a zeolite catalyst and runs the plastic-derived feedstock through a reactor at 550°C or more, producing olefins and aromatics, the basic ingredients for fresh plastics and other chemicals.

EP2937523.headline: Quicker, gentler start-up for steam turbines
EP2937523.summary: Steam turbines must be warmed slowly before full operation, because heating the heavy casing unevenly can damage it, and this delays power generation. Here the casing contains built-in channels that are filled with a hot medium during start-up, so the casing absorbs heat directly and warms more quickly.

EP3360875.headline: New drug compounds against runaway cell growth
EP3360875.summary: Diseases in which cells multiply uncontrollably, notably cancers, need new treatments. This covers a family of chemical compounds, ways of making them, and medicines containing them, intended for treating such disorders. The abstract gives little detail beyond the general chemical structure.

WO2015131821.headline: Clearer sound from small loudspeakers
WO2015131821.summary: Tiny speakers in phones and headphones often distort sound. This design uses a rigid dome mounted on a silicone rubber membrane with a plastic frame, a ring-shaped suspension around the dome, and a very small adhesive-filled gap between the two, aimed at greater sensitivity, less distortion and better sound quality.

US10896053.headline: Stopping virtual servers from multiplying needlessly
US10896053.summary: In cloud computing, new virtual machines are often spun up for every task, wasting resources. This system checks whether existing virtual machines are free to take on work before creating new ones, groups machines by type or location, and balances the workload of the agents that manage them, for instance during backups.

EP3014339.headline: Camera focuses where you are looking
EP3014339.summary: Cameras can struggle to guess which part of a scene the user cares about. This technique tracks the direction of each of the user's eyes, finds where the two lines of sight meet, works out how far that point is from the lens, and focuses the camera there, so the image is sharp where attention is.

EP2963759.headline: Inverter that behaves like a conventional generator
EP2963759.summary: Solar panels, batteries and similar sources feed the grid through power converters, which usually need to lock on to the grid frequency and can trip during disturbances. This converter instead mimics the physics of a traditional spinning generator, including its inertia and voltage control, so it keeps running despite swings in grid voltage or frequency.

EP3129870.headline: Faster machine-learning training on many graphics chips
EP3129870.summary: Training artificial-intelligence models on large datasets is slow on a single processor. This method has the main processor create a separate worker thread for each group of graphics chips, loads batches of training data into their memory, and has them all process data at once, improving the efficiency of multi-chip training.

US9519504.headline: Easier updating of server blueprints
US9519504.summary: Organisations keep template copies of servers so they can create new virtual machines quickly, but templates are awkward to maintain. This approach converts a template into a working virtual machine, carries out maintenance such as updates on it, and then turns it back into template form, keeping the blueprint current with little effort.

US9116873.headline: Automatically tuning stress tests on network equipment
US9116873.summary: Before deployment, network devices are tested by simulating many users to see how they cope under load. This testing platform checks whether the device is handling operations at roughly the target rate and, if not, adds or removes simulated users until it is, making it easier to hit a precise test load.

EP3620534.headline: Tools for precise gene editing
EP3620534.summary: Altering DNA at chosen locations, by deleting, inserting or replacing specific sequences, requires molecular tools that can find and cut the right spot. This covers guide molecules and the complexes they form with cutting enzymes to make such targeted edits, both in an organism's genome and in other genetic material.

WO2014153570.headline: Closed-loop recycling of waste into fuels and materials
WO2014153570.summary: Refining and waste processing usually produce emissions and discarded by-products. This proposes an integrated set of modules that processes varied feedstocks in a sealed, emission-free loop, pre-treating them to separate harmful substances and recover metals, carbon, sulphur, water and gases for energy, while producing refined petroleum products at lower cost.

EP2857983.headline: Teaching computers which fonts look alike
EP2857983.summary: Finding a font that resembles another is hard to automate because similarity is a matter of human judgement. This system collects measurable features of pairs of fonts together with survey results on how similar people find them, and trains a machine-learning model on that data, so it can later judge font similarity itself.

EP2992626.headline: Letting phones talk directly to each other
EP2992626.summary: Nearby mobile devices can communicate directly rather than routing everything through the network, but they need to know which radio resources to use. Here the base station sets aside pools of resources, announces them over a broadcast channel, and allocates specific slots to a device that asks to send direct messages.

EP3667944.headline: Renewing encryption keys on dual-connected phones
EP3667944.summary: A phone may be connected to two base stations at once for higher speeds, each using its own encryption key, which must be refreshed periodically. Here the secondary station asks the main station to refresh its key, the main station instructs the phone, and the phone confirms completion, keeping the link secure without disruption.

EP3163908.headline: Deeper bass from compact speaker modules
EP3163908.summary: Small speakers in phones and portable devices struggle to produce bass. This module adds two passive radiators arranged in parallel to enclose a cavity. Sound from the back of the main speaker's diaphragm is split between them, and the sound inside the cavity is channelled out through a separate opening, improving the bass response.

DE102014009724.headline: Cooler phone charging pad for cars
DE102014009724.summary: Charging a mobile phone in a car can make it overheat. This in-car charger places a wave-shaped element with many openings between the charging unit and the surface the phone rests on, so that cooling air can flow through and carry heat away while the phone charges.

EP3004337.headline: Gene-edited immune cells to fight cancer
EP3004337.summary: Immune cells can be engineered to attack cancer, but treatments usually have to be made from each patient's own cells. This method uses CRISPR/Cas9 gene editing to switch off key genes in donor T-cells so they can be given to any patient, and fits them with receptors that steer them towards cancerous or infected cells, aiming at affordable off-the-shelf immunotherapy.

KR20140117160.headline: Self-cleaning floating solar panels
KR20140117160.summary: Solar panels floating on reservoirs lose output as dust and dirt build up, and are awkward to clean by hand. This system detects how dirty the panels are, partly from their temperature pattern, then pumps water from the reservoir and sprays it over the panels under automatic control to wash them.

WO2015069601.headline: Faster reconnection for dual-SIM phones
WO2015069601.summary: Phones with two SIM cards normally search for a network for each SIM separately, which is slow and drains the battery after switch-on or loss of signal. Here the phone scans once for all available channels, checks whether the strongest matches any SIM's preferred network, and immediately connects that SIM, avoiding repeated searches.

US9270754.headline: Centralised software control for storage networks
US9270754.summary: The networks linking servers to storage arrays in data centres are complex to configure and manage. This method splits their control into a central layer, handling network-wide tasks such as naming, zoning and routing, and local layers on each switch, bringing the flexibility of software-defined networking to storage.

EP3005282.headline: Connected pill box that tracks medicine taking
EP3005282.summary: Patients often forget doses or confuse their pills. This system links a patient's device, a medication storage container with sensors and a display, and a central server, which keep adherence records in step with one another and help identify pills, so that patients and carers can monitor whether medicines are taken as prescribed.

EP3011504.headline: Sorting videos by the faces in them
EP3011504.summary: Automatically categorising videos is hard when the people appearing in them are not known. This method detects a face in a video, matches it against a pool of unidentified faces seen before, finds already-categorised videos that feature the same person, and assigns their categories to the new video.

US10002159.headline: Turning plain keywords into precise database queries
US10002159.summary: People search with a few keywords, but databases answer best to structured queries. This system maps the keywords onto concepts in a specialist vocabulary, links them into a connected graph following known relationships, and converts the result into a formal logic-based query, giving users more relevant results without their learning a query language.

US8933737.headline: Chips that slow down when voltage dips
US8933737.summary: When a chip's power supply briefly dips, it can make errors if it keeps running at full speed. This clock generator watches the supply voltage and, when it drops below a threshold, immediately diverts current from the oscillator to reduce the chip's clock speed, restoring it once the dip has passed.

US11080668.headline: Scanning cheques to settle outstanding invoices
US11080668.summary: Businesses receiving cheques must match them against the invoices being paid, which is tedious when several are outstanding. This system scans a cheque or other payment into an image and applies the credit to the relevant invoices, including those issued by business partners, spreading the payment according to user input or preset rules.

EP3017642.headline: Organising signal measurements in wireless networks
EP3017642.summary: Wireless networks ask devices to measure signal conditions and report back, which can create a lot of traffic. This arrangement assigns devices to measurement groups announced in a broadcast message, and triggers their reports with a specific request message, giving the network a more orderly way to gather the data it needs.

EP3037657.headline: Wind farms that weigh wear against output
EP3037657.summary: In a wind farm, turbulence from an upwind turbine reduces the output of those behind it, and settings can be adjusted to limit this. Using wind forecasts, this method calculates the extra power from adjusting the upwind turbine, weighs it against the fatigue the change inflicts, and only makes the change when the gain outweighs the cost.

WO2015009748.headline: Surround sound that tunes itself to the room
WO2015009748.summary: Surround sound only works well if the system knows where the speakers and the listener are. Here a microphone array built into the front speaker or soundbar plays a test signal through each speaker to locate it, and listens for the listener's voice to find their position, then adjusts each speaker accordingly.

WO2015005655.headline: Reliable wiring for nano-scale LEDs
WO2015005655.summary: Light-emitting diodes only nanometres in size are hard to connect to electrodes without faults. This design lays the tiny LEDs flat and links them to two electrodes on the same surface, rather than standing them upright between layers, with a coating to prevent short circuits, improving light output and cutting defect rates.

WO2015010129.headline: Rebuilding clean speech from noisy recordings
WO2015010129.summary: Background noise makes speech hard to understand for both people and machines. Rather than merely filtering the noise, this approach analyses the recording in the way the human ear processes sound, picks out the features belonging to the speaker, and uses them to synthesise fresh, clean speech with the same pitch and tone.

US9846946.headline: Picking out poles and trees in 3D scans
US9846946.summary: Laser scans of streets produce vast clouds of 3D points that are hard to interpret automatically. This method first strips out the ground and buildings using an unsupervised technique, then applies a trained recogniser to what remains to identify upright objects such as poles and trees, useful for mapping and navigation.

EP3080124.headline: New compounds to calm overactive immune responses
EP3080124.summary: In autoimmune and inflammatory diseases such as lupus, rheumatoid arthritis and psoriasis, parts of the immune system fire when they should not. These compounds block certain toll-like receptors, which act as immune alarm triggers, and are intended as medicines to prevent or treat such conditions.

WO2016054957.headline: Spotting crashing apps on a phone cheaply
WO2016054957.summary: Detecting when an app on a phone is misbehaving usually means constant monitoring that drains the battery. This method only checks when particular system events occur, looks for processes that have restarted, counts how often each restarts within a set period, and flags an app as faulty if it exceeds a threshold.

WO2015016004.headline: Compact zoom lens design for cameras
WO2015016004.summary: Zoom lenses must balance size against image quality. This design uses three groups of lens elements, with specific rules for how each group moves while zooming and for the ratios of their optical powers, allowing a compact lens with good performance across the zoom range, for use in cameras and interchangeable lens barrels.

WO2015020623.headline: Well cement made with refinery waste
WO2015020623.summary: Oil and gas wells are lined with cement to seal off rock layers, stop gas migrating and protect the well against corrosion. This cement mix incorporates spent catalyst left over from oil-refinery cracking processes, giving a use to a waste product while providing the sealing and integrity needed underground.

EP3055813.headline: Stabler trial-and-error learning for AI
EP3055813.summary: Reinforcement learning teaches software to act by rewarding good decisions, but training with neural networks can be unstable. Here experience gathered by acting on the system trains one network, while the targets it learns from come from a second network that is a periodically updated copy of the first, which steadies learning.

EP3660050.headline: Antibodies targeting an immune-cell brake
EP3660050.summary: LAG-3 is a molecule found on immune cells that acts as a brake on their activity. These antibody molecules bind specifically to LAG-3 and are intended for use in treating, preventing or diagnosing cancers and infectious diseases.

WO2015058019.headline: Instant rerouting when an internet gateway fails
WO2015058019.summary: When a router at the edge of a core network fails, traffic can be lost while the network finds another path. This method chooses a primary and a backup edge router in advance, and writes both into each data packet's header, so packets can be switched to the backup immediately if the primary becomes unavailable.

EP3298273.headline: Wind farms that help steady grid frequency
EP3298273.summary: Grids need generators that can instantly boost output when frequency drops, a job wind farms do poorly if turbines are simply held back by a fixed margin. This method plans the whole farm's frequency support and power output together in one optimisation, allowing for wake effects between turbines and wind forecasts.

EP3072036.headline: Digital handwriting strokes you can slice and share
EP3072036.summary: Pen input on screens is captured as a series of positions that must be turned into smooth strokes and exchanged between apps. This method records pen-down, movement and pen-up events as control points for smooth curves, and tags each stroke with two values marking which part to display, allowing strokes to be partially shown or cut.

EP3080774.headline: Matching ride requests to drivers in batches
EP3080774.summary: Ride-hailing apps usually assign the nearest free driver to each request as it arrives, which is not always best overall. This system considers several open requests in an area at once, identifies drivers who could reach them within a set time, and chooses assignments that minimise waiting time for pick-up.

EP3140809.headline: Flagging trouble spots during dental scans
EP3140809.summary: Dentists increasingly scan patients' mouths to create 3D models, but problem areas can be missed during the scan. This method spots a possible area of interest in one scan image, confirms it by comparing with a second image, and alerts the dentist while the scan is still under way.

US9612910.headline: Quicker indexing of storage backups
US9612910.summary: Backup systems take snapshots of data volumes and build catalogues so files can be found, but cataloguing each snapshot from scratch is slow. This method asks the storage vendor's software which blocks changed between two snapshots and updates the earlier catalogue accordingly, generating the new catalogue without a full rescan.

EP3084760.headline: Wake-word listening without draining the battery
EP3084760.summary: Voice assistants need to listen constantly, but running full speech recognition all the time uses too much power. Here a small low-power chip listens for a trigger phrase while the main processor sleeps; on hearing it, the chip wakes the main processor and hands over the audio captured after the phrase, so no words are lost.

US10446498.headline: Safer electrical separation inside chip packages
US10446498.summary: Some circuits must exchange signals while remaining electrically isolated, for safety or to cope with different voltages. This arrangement puts two chips and a capacitive isolation circuit together inside one moulded package, with the isolation circuit sitting outside both chips, letting them communicate without a direct electrical connection.

EP3109986.headline: Power regulator that extends battery life
EP3109986.summary: Voltage regulators in battery-powered devices waste some current even at rest. This design has a controller that feeds a secondary power domain either from the main supply or from the regulator's own output, depending on the output voltage, reducing the idle current drawn from the battery and prolonging its life.

US10496947.headline: Reading call-centre agents' emotions on video
US10496947.summary: Managers want to measure how well customer-service staff perform during video calls. This system detects an agent's face in the video, fits a virtual mesh to it, tracks how the mesh deforms over time to recognise facial emotions, and converts these into work-quality metrics intended for workforce management.

EP3164471.headline: Turning wood and crop waste into fuel
EP3164471.summary: Solid biomass could replace fossil oil as a fuel source if it can be converted efficiently. This two-stage process first heats the biomass with hydrogen over a partially sulphided metal catalyst to strip out most of the oxygen, removes the char, then treats the vapour over a second catalyst to produce hydrocarbons similar to conventional fuels.

US9940114.headline: Quality seals that control software roll-outs
US9940114.summary: Installing software into the wrong environment causes failures. This approach attaches a quality-assurance seal to each software package listing the hardware, middleware and applications it needs. Deployment is authorised only where the seal exactly matches a registered seal and the environment's details, and is refused where no match exists.

WO2016176981.headline: Simpler, better-sealed loudspeaker assembly
WO2016176981.summary: Small loudspeaker modules for phones are fiddly to assemble and often poorly sealed. This design gives the speaker's shell a surface that is welded to the module's outer shell using ultrasound, along a matching weld line, cutting assembly steps, improving the seal and appearance, and lowering production costs.

WO2016165355.headline: Richer sound from phone speakers using absorbent grains
WO2016165355.summary: Compact loudspeakers sound better if the chamber behind them is acoustically larger. Here the rear cavity is filled with fine non-foaming sound-absorbing particles, held away from the speaker itself by mesh dividers, so the cavity can be filled as fully as possible and the particles' absorbing effect fully used, at low production cost.

US9535236.headline: Slim six-element camera lens for gadgets
US9535236.summary: Cameras in phones and other thin devices need lenses that are very short yet still sharp. This lens uses six elements arranged from the scene side to the sensor side, with their surface shapes and optical parameters chosen so that the overall length is short while image quality remains good.

EP3026635.headline: Less wasted effort in mobile graphics rendering
EP3026635.summary: Graphics chips in phones draw scenes tile by tile, and adding fine surface detail through tessellation is expensive. This design builds tessellation into both the stage that sorts objects into tiles and the stage that renders them, and offers an efficiency mode that defers or reduces tessellation, saving processing power.

WO2015166408.headline: Hybrid rice boosts fish and shrimp farming
WO2015166408.summary: Fish, shrimp or prawns can be raised in the same flooded fields as rice. This method improves the yield of those aquatic animals by growing hybrid rice varieties in such combined rice-and-aquaculture systems rather than conventional rice.

US11243898.headline: Smarter traffic control for computer memory
US11243898.summary: Memory chips are divided into regions, and the order in which pending read and write requests are handled affects speed and energy use. This controller keeps a compact summary of which requests are waiting for each region, and consults it when deciding what commands to send, avoiding the cost of scanning the whole queue.

WO2015126664.headline: Building taller stacks of memory cells
WO2015126664.summary: Flash memory stores more by stacking cells vertically, but very tall stacks are hard to make in one go. This manufacturing method builds a lower stack of conductive and insulating layers with stepped edges and memory channels, then adds a second stack on top, forming connected channels through both, to increase storage density.

WO2015127083.headline: Efficient copying of data to backup servers
WO2015127083.summary: Keeping a replica of a storage volume on another server means copying a lot of data. This method forwards new writes to the replica as they happen while tracking what has been written, compares the source's metadata with an earlier snapshot to find changed blocks, and fetches only those not already received.

EP2985711.headline: Automatically mining medical records for drug safety
EP2985711.summary: Monitoring the safety of medicines means sifting through huge volumes of medical records and clinical literature. This system automatically reads such text, extracts facts and relationships, forms a preliminary clinical judgement, and generates reports, which clinicians and medical experts then check, speeding up drug-safety monitoring.

EP3295741.headline: Phones allocating radio capacity to each other
EP3295741.summary: Devices communicating directly with one another need to agree which radio resources to use. In this method, one device sends another the configuration for direct communication; the second asks for resources, the first chooses and grants them, and the second then transmits over the allocated resource.

EP3117590.headline: Seamless handover when a data-stream server fails
EP3117590.summary: Systems that process continuous streams of events must not lose or duplicate data when a server fails and a standby takes over. Here the newly active machine identifies the last event block its predecessor published, selects the next one from stored data, and carries on publishing from exactly that point.

US9130563.headline: Chip input circuits that adapt to signal types
US9130563.summary: Programmable chips must accept signals of different electrical standards. This receiver has two input circuits, each with pull-up and pull-down branches and its own enable control, feeding a shared output stage that passes on whichever is active, allowing the chip to be configured for the type of signal it receives.

WO2015142765.headline: Easier and safer bitcoin accounts
WO2015142765.summary: Holding and spending bitcoin is cumbersome and risky for ordinary users. This system lets people send bitcoin to an email address with no miner's fee, keeps most funds in a vault whose private key is split for security, requires several approvals to withdraw, lets merchants lock in local-currency prices, and provides an exchange and a tipping button.

EP3308238.headline: Thermostat that targets comfort, not just temperature
EP3308238.summary: A room feels comfortable depending on humidity, air movement, clothing and activity, not temperature alone. This thermostat controller starts from an initial setting, works out values for those factors using a standard comfort model, then adjusts the temperature setting until predicted comfort reaches a chosen level, and uses that as the target.

US9665153.headline: Processors pick sleep modes more wisely
US9665153.summary: Before a processor enters a deep sleep state it must write out the contents of its shared cache, which takes time. This design calculates how long that flush would take based on the current state of the cache, so the power controller can choose a low-power mode that is actually worthwhile.

EP3089034.headline: Predicting chip workload to save energy
EP3089034.summary: Processors save power by lowering their speed and voltage when demand is light, but they need to anticipate demand. This system builds several forecasting models from the processor's recent workload history, tests which predicts best against what actually happened, and uses the most accurate one to adjust speed and voltage.

EP3201695.headline: Smart lights that let occupants adjust their surroundings
EP3201695.summary: Occupants of shared buildings often cannot easily adjust lighting or other conditions in their space. Here networked light fittings broadcast identification codes, for example encoded in their light. A user's device picks up the code, records the user's preferences, and sends a request to a central manager, which commands the fittings to adjust the environment.

EP3122845.headline: Cooking biomass into crude bio-oil
EP3122845.summary: Plant matter can be turned into an oil substitute, but existing processes are costly. This method heats a slurry of biomass and a water-soluble catalyst at 200 to 350°C under high pressure to produce crude bio-oil, separates the oil, and then recovers the catalyst from the water for reuse.

EP3122402.headline: Injection pen with clearer dose clicks
EP3122402.summary: People injecting insulin and similar medicines set doses on a pen by turning a dial, and mistakes are easy. This pen reduces friction in the dial, gives a louder click for each unit dialled up and a quieter click when a dose is dialled back down, and signals when the cartridge's last dose is reached.

EP3207432.headline: Answering operators' questions about plant equipment
EP3207432.summary: Large process plants run on distributed control systems with information scattered across many databases. This method lets an operator pose a standard type of query about a subsystem's operation or health at the control screen; a server identifies which database holds the relevant information, processes the query, and the system then adjusts the subsystem's process settings.

EP2939456.headline: Securing phones linked to two base stations
EP2939456.summary: Phones can connect to two base stations at once to boost speed, but data sent via the secondary station needs its own protection. This system sets up a security relationship between the phone and the secondary station through signalling via the main station when several cells are added together, and watches the data channels for intruders.

EP2999297.headline: Extending Bluetooth range through device relays
EP2999297.summary: Bluetooth Low Energy devices in a smart home can only reach others within a short range. This system lets some devices act as relay nodes in a mesh network, passing messages on to devices that would otherwise be out of reach, so a whole building can be covered using low-power Bluetooth.

EP3131588.headline: Drug molecules that make cells destroy unwanted proteins
EP3131588.summary: Many diseases involve proteins that are hard to block with conventional drugs. These two-ended molecules grab a target protein with one end and, with the other, bind cereblon, part of the cell's own protein-disposal machinery, bringing the two together so the cell breaks down the target. The approach could apply to almost any protein.

EP3018946.headline: Waking sleeping devices just as data arrives
EP3018946.summary: Battery-powered connected devices sleep for long stretches and only wake briefly, so servers do not know when they can be reached. This method has the mobile network tell an application service shortly before a device's timer expires that it is about to become available, so the service can deliver its data then.

WO2017060488.headline: New compounds to block the TRPA1 channel
WO2017060488.summary: Some diseases and conditions could be eased by blocking a cell channel called TRPA1. This covers a family of chemical compounds that act as TRPA1 antagonists, how to make them, and their use in treating conditions that respond to such blocking. The abstract gives few further details.

EP3140780.headline: Smart glasses that keep checking who's wearing them
EP3140780.summary: Wearable headsets can display sensitive information, so they need to be sure who is wearing them. This system uses cameras pointed at the eyes to recognise the wearer's iris, and other physical or behavioural cues, continuously in real time. The verified identity can lock or unlock secure content and be sent to remote systems to set security measures.

EP3139320.headline: Picking the right tests for software bug reports
EP3139320.summary: When software fails in use, teams must work out which tests to run to reproduce and fix the problem. This system reads an incident ticket with machine learning, picks out keywords, locates where the problem lies, finds the matching test workspace and relevant test cases, and either runs them or learns from how staff handled the ticket manually.

WO2017041372.headline: Chatbot that routes requests to specialist services
WO2017041372.summary: Keyword search is a stilted way to interact with computers. This system takes a user's natural-language request, works out their intent, forwards the request to one or more specialised service subsystems, and combines their replies according to preset rules into a single answer, allowing chat-like, multi-turn conversations closer to talking with a person.

JP2015197615.headline: Multi-lens camera that focuses all lenses at once
JP2015197615.summary: Cameras with several lenses of different focal lengths can capture wide and zoomed views simultaneously, but keeping every lens in focus is difficult. In this compact design each lens system has a moving focus group at the front and a fixed group behind, with neighbouring focus lenses shaped differently and focal lengths kept within a set ratio.

US9602345.headline: Data-driven tuning of Wi-Fi access points
US9602345.summary: Wireless access points have many adjustable settings, and it is unclear which matter most for performance. This system gathers real-time data from many access points, builds a predictive model of performance, ranks the influencing factors by their impact, and then automatically adjusts the settings that matter most.

WO2017031861.headline: Speaker that also delivers vibration alerts
WO2017031861.summary: Small devices often need both a loudspeaker and a vibration motor, which take up space. This device combines them: a flat voice coil drives a diaphragm for sound, while the magnet and an added weight are suspended on a ring-shaped spring inside the housing, allowing the unit to act as a vibrator as well.

EP3219098.headline: Video meetings with life-like 3D participants
EP3219098.summary: Ordinary video calls show flat images and give little sense of presence. This system captures a 3D image stream of a participant and reconstructs it inside a virtual window in a computer-generated meeting room, so they appear as a three-dimensional presence. Other participants can appear in further windows or as avatars.

WO2015188678.headline: Smoother mobile video over patchy networks
WO2015188678.summary: Video streamed from a phone stutters when the network fluctuates. This method continuously measures network conditions, weighs them against a table of thresholds, and adjusts frame rate, bit rate and resolution, as well as the wireless chip's settings, to keep delay low. It also makes sure the key frames essential to picture quality get through.

EP3879881.headline: Phones asking for a better radio beam
EP3879881.summary: Newer mobile networks send signals in narrow directional beams, which can weaken as a user moves. Here the device measures the quality of reference signals on its beam and, if it stays below a threshold for several readings, asks the base station to switch to a beam pair it recommends, then adjusts its antenna to receive on the new beam.

JP2015225102.headline: Thin phone camera lens with less glare
JP2015225102.summary: Slim phone cameras with wide apertures tend to suffer from ghosting and flare caused by stray light. This lens of five or more elements puts a light-blocking film on the outer rim of the first or second lens, outside the area that forms the image, stopping unwanted light without adding a separate shield.

WO2016090301.headline: Precisely scoring solar cells for cutting
WO2016090301.summary: Solar cells are often scored so they can be divided into strips. This system moves a solar cell along a conveyor past a scribing tool that cuts a groove to a set depth; in one version the groove stops short of the junction between the cell's two active layers.

WO2016090332.headline: Solar cell contacts designed for overlapping strips
WO2016090332.summary: Solar cells can be overlapped like roof shingles to form a panel, but the overlap can hide the electrical contacts. This electrode layout combines thin finger lines and an edge busbar with contact pads positioned so that, when one cell is cascaded over its neighbour, the pads remain at least partly exposed for connection.

EP3409669.headline: New drugs targeting faulty cell-signalling enzymes
EP3409669.summary: Enzymes called kinases control signalling within cells, and faulty versions of two of them, EGFR and HER2, are linked to disease. These compounds and medicines based on them are designed to modulate kinase activity, including that of mutant EGFR and HER2, for treating the associated diseases and conditions.

WO2016007672.headline: 3D printing that heats whole layers at once
WO2016007672.summary: Most metal and plastic 3D printers fuse material with a single scanning beam, which is slow. This system deposits feed material on a platform under computer control and heats it across an entire layer, or a strip spanning the platform's width that sweeps along its length, using an array of heat lamps or a plasma source.

WO2016108791.headline: Dishwasher with water reservoirs for reuse
WO2016108791.summary: Dishwashers use a lot of fresh water. This design adds two tanks beneath the washing tub, one holding water from the washing stage and one holding rinse water, connected by a pipe with a valve, a layout that allows water to be transferred between the two stages.

WO2016090304.headline: Robot squirts glue onto solar cells precisely
WO2016090304.summary: Solar panels are built by joining many small cells with conductive glue, and getting the right amount in exactly the right place by hand is slow and error-prone. Here a robotic arm carries a jet dispenser that sprays a measured dose onto each cell's metal strips without touching them, lining itself up automatically.

EP3172838.headline: Mapping signal echoes to speed up wireless data
EP3172838.summary: Radio, cable and fibre links are muddied by echoes and frequency shifts caused by reflections. The method sends short test bursts to build a detailed two-dimensional picture of these distortions, then uses that picture to tune transmission, turning the flaws into extra capacity. It aims at more robust, higher-speed wireless networks.

WO2016090339.headline: Heated bars cure glue joining solar strips
WO2016090339.summary: Modern solar panels are made from overlapping strips stuck together with conductive paste that must be heated to set. Two heated bars press onto the top and bottom of each overlap and warm it to about 160 degrees Celsius, curing just the joint rather than the whole panel, for faster, more consistent manufacturing.

EP3175440.headline: Rollable screen that stiffens when flat
EP3175440.summary: Flexible screens need support so they do not sag, yet must also bend to roll away. A backing panel stays rigid when flat but is locally softened by an actuator just where it passes round a roller, bending there and stiffening again once past, allowing a display to roll up and unroll.

WO2016021235.headline: Games that react to when you sleep
WO2016021235.summary: Sleep-tracking apps usually make users enter data or start things manually. This system gathers sleep information automatically, works out when a person has woken or got out of bed, and lets a game or other app respond to those moments without extra effort from the user.

EP3240714.headline: Self-driving cars that learn your driving style
EP3240714.summary: Passengers may find a self-driving car's style too timid or too brisk. The car loads a chosen driver profile to govern how it behaves in autonomous mode, then watches sensor data while the person drives manually and adjusts the profile to mimic that personal style, making automated driving feel more familiar.

WO2016032892.headline: Use your wristwatch to control smart glasses
WO2016032892.summary: Smart glasses are awkward to control without a keyboard or touchscreen. The headset recognises the wearer's watch, projects a virtual menu onto it, and tracks the wearer's taps and gestures on the watch to move through that menu, turning an ordinary watch into a controller for augmented-reality content.

EP3183843.headline: Spotting malware by its random web addresses
EP3183843.summary: Some malware generates streams of gibberish web addresses to find its controllers while evading blacklists. The method watches for failed address lookups, scores each failed name on length, structure and complexity, groups suspicious ones, and then flags any that later succeed as likely command servers. It helps network security teams detect infected machines.

WO2016116878.headline: Antibiotic combination to beat resistant bacteria
WO2016116878.summary: Bacteria increasingly defeat cephalosporin antibiotics by producing enzymes that break them down. The composition pairs a cephalosporin with a new compound that blocks those enzymes, aiming to restore the antibiotic's effectiveness against resistant infections.

EP3139313.headline: Learning what normal looks like to flag anomalies
EP3139313.summary: Spotting faults or unusual events in streams of sensor or business data is hard when normal behaviour varies. The system learns from one reference data series how large prediction errors typically are, then applies those learned limits to a second series and raises an alert when errors fall outside them.

WO2016036401.headline: Patients set rules for sharing their data
WO2016036401.summary: Health and other sensitive records are often shared in ways that ignore laws, consent agreements and personal wishes. This system encodes those rules in layers, lets patients choose who sees which fields and in what context, and links differently labelled fields across organisations so that permitted data can be queried consistently.

US9984006.headline: Software learns which files need encrypting
US9984006.summary: Deciding which documents contain sensitive material and should be encrypted is laborious. The system is shown sample files known to be sensitive, reads their content with language-processing tools and derives rules describing them. It then applies those rules to new files to decide automatically whether each should be encrypted.

WO2016044413.headline: Routing business traffic over the best link
WO2016044413.summary: Different applications need different network performance, while link quality changes constantly. The method works out what an application requires, picks the most suitable connection at that moment according to a policy and current conditions, and routes the application's traffic over it.

EP3133539.headline: Software robots for routine office tasks
EP3133539.summary: Many business tasks involve repetitive reading from documents and typing into applications. This process automation software records and replays keyboard and mouse actions across different systems and platforms, handles unexpected errors, keeps an audit log, and lets administrators configure it without a separate maintenance interface.

EP3067827.headline: Car spots distracted drivers and intervenes
EP3067827.summary: Distraction causes many road accidents. The car's computer receives camera images from the driver's phone to judge their state, combines this with vehicle data such as speed, grades how serious the distraction is, and then takes a matching action, from a gentle alert to controlling vehicle systems.

EP3268076.headline: Safer catheter with built-in leak-proof valves
EP3268076.summary: Intravenous catheters with a side port for injections can leak or let blood flow back. This design places a valve inside the hub with two parts, one for the side port and one for the main inlet, which open only when a syringe or similar device is pushed in.

EP3198421.headline: Rules decide which gadgets may join networks
EP3198421.summary: Organisations must securely admit laptops and phones as well as unattended devices such as sensors and printers. The system detects a device joining the network, works out its type, applies the matching enrolment policy and rules, and admits it only if it meets the required criteria.

WO2016048447.headline: Telling computer memory which requests matter most
WO2016048447.summary: In a computer, urgent and routine requests for data compete for memory. This framework attaches a priority to each memory request and passes it down through the memory hierarchy so that the memory system can serve the most important requests first, improving responsiveness.

EP3197287.headline: Gelatine-free sweets using seaweed extract
EP3197287.summary: Gummy sweets usually rely on gelatine, an animal product many consumers avoid. A low-viscosity form of iota carrageenan, a seaweed-derived thickener, is used to replace some or all of the gelatine while keeping the familiar chewy texture.

EP3193257.headline: Trimming duplicate tests in software projects
EP3193257.summary: Large software test suites accumulate duplicated and overlapping test cases that cost time to run and maintain. The method removes redundant cases, measures how similar the remaining ones are by comparing their descriptions and steps, groups them, extracts reusable test functions, and rewrites the cases to reference those shared functions.

EP3065085.headline: Teams of neural networks identify objects in photos
EP3065085.summary: A single neural network can misclassify objects in images. The method builds many networks with different designs and settings, keeps those that pass a validation threshold, and combines their predictions so the group as a whole labels objects in a picture more accurately.

EP3206170.headline: Software learns to automate tasks by watching screens
EP3206170.summary: Setting up software robots for office tasks usually needs manual scripting. Here a monitoring program takes screenshots of an application, uses image processing to recognise buttons and fields, records sequences of user clicks, identifies which sequences led to success, and builds an automation model from them on demand.

US9941207.headline: Faster, higher-yield stacking of computer chips
US9941207.summary: Stacked three-dimensional chip packages are slow to make and a single faulty layer can ruin the whole stack. The method builds the two wiring layers on separate production lines in parallel, tests each layer, and only combines known-good layers and chips, cutting cycle time and waste.

EP3280446.headline: Easier-to-take forms of a leukaemia drug
EP3280446.summary: Ibrutinib treats blood cancers such as lymphoma and chronic lymphocytic leukaemia. These oral formulations put the drug in capsules, sprinkle capsules or a liquid suspension, with specified inactive ingredients, to make it easier to prepare and take.

EP3212189.headline: New compounds to treat cystic fibrosis
EP3212189.summary: Cystic fibrosis and some lung and pancreatic conditions stem from a faulty protein called CFTR. A new family of chemical compounds acts on this protein and may be formulated into medicines for these diseases.

US9336483.headline: Self-updating AI for online learning platforms
US9336483.summary: Online education and content platforms use predictive models that go stale as users and material change. This system builds and trains neural networks, monitors how well they perform, and continuously trains replacement candidates in the cloud, swapping them in when they do better.

WO2016074048.headline: Simpler way to build heat exchanger cores
WO2016074048.summary: Heat exchangers transfer warmth between fluids through stacks of plates. The core is made by placing spacers between flat plates, stacking them in order into a block and welding the block together; in one version hollow spacers themselves act as the separating surfaces, dispensing with the plates.

WO2016075588.headline: More stable form of a hepatitis C drug
WO2016075588.summary: Daclatasvir is a hepatitis C medicine whose solid form affects shelf life and manufacture. A stable non-crystalline form of its dihydrochloride salt, and the process for making it, is provided.

US9348450.headline: Hinge that keeps folding screens flat and firm
US9348450.summary: Foldable phone screens tend to feel soft at the crease when open and can be damaged if folded too tightly. Two rotating plates slide against supports from the rigid parts of the screen, holding the crease firm when open and spreading apart when folded so the screen bends in a gentle curve.

EP3295643.headline: Secure tunnel for individual phone apps
EP3295643.summary: Companies want work apps on employees' phones to reach private networks without routing the whole phone through a corporate connection. The phone intercepts a given app's network requests, opens a dedicated encrypted link to a VPN server, and forwards only that app's traffic to the private network.

EP3227799.headline: Watchdog that tells when AI models go stale
EP3227799.summary: Predictive models used for scoring consumers can degrade as the world changes. An auto-encoder, a type of neural network, learns what typical data looks like; when it struggles to reconstruct new data, the model is likely unsuitable, signalling a rebuild, choosing among models, or flagging unusual groups of customers.

EP3101599.headline: Test bench for comparing machine-learning methods
EP3101599.summary: Choosing the best machine-learning approach for a dataset usually means laborious trial and error. This system holds a library of algorithms, trains and evaluates each selected model on a dataset, and aggregates the results into comparison statistics presented to the user.

WO2017207712.headline: Machine hangs safety nets on tunnel walls
WO2017207712.summary: Lining tunnel ceilings and walls with protective netting is dangerous and slow by hand. A mobile machine carries a movable arm ending in a curved panel that holds the unrolled net against the tunnel surface while it is fixed in place.

WO2016193337.headline: Cleaning waste water from synthetic fuel plants
WO2016193337.summary: Plants that turn natural gas or coal-bed methane into liquid fuels via the Fischer-Tropsch process produce large volumes of contaminated water as a by-product. A treatment method is provided for this waste water stream.

EP3235295.headline: Phones pick the best neighbour to relay signals
EP3235295.summary: In 5G networks a phone with poor coverage can route traffic through a nearby device acting as a relay. The phone listens for relays announcing themselves, measures the link quality to each and considers how well each relay connects to the base station, then chooses the best one.

WO2016109607.headline: Earphones that listen for cues and offer deals
WO2016109607.summary: Audio devices such as earphones capture a user's surroundings and detect spoken keywords. Combined with context, these reveal what the person wants or needs, and a service provider can respond with a reminder, advert, coupon or discount, possibly only when the user reaches a particular location.

WO2016108909.headline: Better underground rock analysis for oil drilling
WO2016108909.summary: Oil and gas firms need to know what rock and fluids surround a borehole. An electromagnetic tool lowered down the well takes multi-directional measurements, which are fitted to a model allowing rock properties to differ by direction, yielding logs of water content, rock type and minerals such as pyrite.

EP3310772.headline: New drug compounds targeting gene-reading proteins
EP3310772.summary: Bromodomain proteins help switch genes on and are implicated in cancers and inflammatory diseases. A new family of chemical compounds blocks these proteins and may be developed into treatments for conditions where such blocking is beneficial.

WO2016204832.headline: USB-C chips that sip power while idle
WO2016204832.summary: USB-C connectors must keep watching for a cable even when the device sleeps, draining the battery. This chip design runs the necessary detection circuits in a deep-sleep state using no more than 100 microamps, extending standby time for phones, laptops and accessories.

EP3317266.headline: New drug compounds targeting gene-reading proteins
EP3317266.summary: Bromodomain proteins help switch genes on and are implicated in cancers and inflammatory diseases. A new class of two-ring chemical compounds blocks these proteins and may be developed into treatments for conditions where such blocking is beneficial.

EP3118807.headline: Deciding which IT problems to automate first
EP3118807.summary: IT departments face many recurring issues but cannot automate all of them at once. The method maps how each issue is handled, weighs the cost, quality and risk of automating it, ranks the candidates, and produces a prioritised plan and business case for automation.

EP4597302.headline: Platform for building industrial internet-of-things apps
EP4597302.summary: Companies with sensors across factories, grids or fleets struggle to combine streams of readings with conventional business records. This platform ingests both, stores each in a suitable database, aggregates them into a common analytical store, and presents a unified data model on which software applications can be built.

US9678539.headline: Pull-apart device reveals bigger screen
US9678539.summary: Small devices limit screen size. Here a flexible display is housed inside two bodies joined by rotating arms; pulling the bodies apart draws out more of the screen, so the visible display area grows and shrinks with the distance between them.

EP3118783.headline: Forecasting wind farm output with trained models
EP3118783.summary: Grid operators need to know how much power a wind farm will generate. The system combines weather and turbine data, selects from a range of forecasting models, trains them on recent data and runs them to predict electricity production, helping plan supply and sales.

US10014060.headline: Protecting flash memory from heavy-reading wear
US10014060.summary: Repeatedly reading the same area of flash memory can corrupt neighbouring data. The controller counts reads per block, identifies the data being read most often, and moves it to a more durable block until demand falls, reducing errors in solid-state drives and memory cards.

WO2016130533.headline: Helmet lights adjust to your eyes
WO2016130533.summary: Fixed-brightness helmet lights can dazzle or prove too dim as conditions change. The helmet measures outside light and the wearer's pupil size, and adjusts the built-in light's intensity accordingly.

EP3256929.headline: Processor shifts work to save energy
EP3256929.summary: Multicore processors waste power running memory-heavy tasks on general-purpose cores. Counters in each core report what kind of work is running; a power controller identifies the workload type and moves suitable threads to a specialised core for the next interval, lowering energy use.

US9785764.headline: Checking digital ID without exposing personal data
US9785764.summary: Proving identity online or in person often reveals more than necessary. A device scans a bearer's digital credential and sends it, with its own credential, to a validation service, which confirms both, returns only the requested detail, and issues fresh one-time credentials to both parties to limit reuse and fraud.

EP3259920.headline: Sharpening blurry video using neighbouring frames
EP3259920.summary: Low-quality video looks poor on large screens. The method takes several neighbouring frames of low-resolution footage, extracts features from them with a layered algorithm, and uses that information to enhance a target frame, producing clearer pictures from compressed or low-bandwidth video.

WO2016138178.headline: Control smart glasses with your gaze
WO2016138178.summary: Headsets lack convenient buttons. A sensor tracks where the wearer is looking; when the gaze lands on a predefined trigger zone, a virtual object or menu appears, letting the user select and activate features with eye movement alone.

US9432025.headline: Keeping chip clock signals in step
US9432025.summary: Digital chips rely on multiple clock signals that must tick in step; small timing offsets cause errors. A circuit measures the phase difference between two clocks and nudges them into alignment once they are within the measurement's error margin.

EP3262815.headline: Cloud security blanket for company IT systems
EP3262815.summary: Companies spread across many cloud services struggle to see and protect their users, apps and data. A cloud security fabric connects to the firm's infrastructure and cloud platforms, gathers security-relevant events, and offers services such as selective encryption, automated policies, content classification and user behaviour analytics.

WO2017197832.headline: Parked cars top up their own battery
WO2017197832.summary: Vehicles left standing for long periods can drain their 12-volt battery. A controller enters a low-power timer, wakes at set intervals to check the battery voltage, and if it is below a threshold uses the main battery via a converter to recharge it, preventing a flat battery.

US9779233.headline: Single sign-on across different web domains
US9779233.summary: Users logging into an application hosted in one domain often need their identity confirmed by a provider in another. After the identity provider vouches for the user, the system picks two random keys, blends them into a secret, signs the user's details to create a token, checks it and grants access.

US10055267.headline: Avoiding failure clusters in flash storage
US10055267.summary: In flash memory, bad blocks often come in clusters within one physical region, so drawing fresh blocks from one area can cause a run of write errors. The memory is divided into zones and new free blocks are taken from zones in rotation, spreading the risk.

US9926852.headline: Choosing the cheapest way to run gas turbines
US9926852.summary: Power plants with several gas turbines can meet a given output in many combinations. Using current readings from each turbine, the method defines competing operating modes, predicts each one's performance over a period, costs them with a cost function, and selects the cheapest.

EP3271891.headline: Upgrading factory control systems without stopping
EP3271891.summary: Updating software in industrial control systems usually means halting production. New software is installed on a virtual machine server, which temporarily takes over from an existing control device; the virtual machine is then converted back onto physical hardware, either the original or a new device.

EP3939446.headline: Heat-not-burn tobacco device using induction heating
EP3939446.summary: Devices that heat tobacco without burning it need a heater that warms the material evenly. A varying magnetic field is generated around a chamber holding the tobacco, heating an elongated metal element that surrounds the chamber and releases the flavour vapours.

WO2016155564.headline: Image recognition that works at any size
WO2016155564.summary: Image-recognising neural networks typically require inputs of a fixed size. By adding a horizontal pooling step after each convolution layer during training, the resulting model captures features along the image's width and can recognise images of any size, broadening where it can be used.

US10185821.headline: Risk scores for suspicious user behaviour
US10185821.summary: Security teams need to spot insiders or accounts behaving oddly. The system runs search queries over machine-generated event logs for users on a watch list, compares the results against a statistical baseline, and when a trigger condition is met raises the user's risk score and shows it on a dashboard.

EP3357011.headline: Planning maintenance work more efficiently
EP3357011.summary: Industries such as mining, oil and gas, chemicals and transport must plan, schedule and coordinate many maintenance jobs. The system supports defining, planning and scheduling these field-service activities to optimise how they are carried out.

EP3292484.headline: Proving your identity using a blockchain
EP3292484.summary: Verifying identity documents online is slow and vulnerable to forgery. A device reads personal data from an ID card, creates a digital fingerprint of it, signs it and stores the signature on a public blockchain. A second party can then check that the data presented matches the recorded fingerprint and signature.

EP3174175.headline: Monitor warns when batteries become unsafe
EP3174175.summary: Ageing battery packs can fail dangerously. A monitor measures the pack's voltage before and after a charge or discharge cycle, waits for it to settle, divides the voltage change by the charge passed to estimate the pack's health, displays the result and disconnects the pack if health falls below a limit.

JP2016184901.headline: Magnetic rubber that resists wear in actuators
JP2016184901.summary: Rubber supports in magnetic actuators can creep and deform as they age, letting the moving part drift. A polymer containing fine magnetic particles, sized so they respond faster than the alternating magnetic field, forms a support that carries the magnetic circuit without hindering motion or degrading.

EP3295508.headline: Longer-lasting batteries with silicon electrodes
EP3295508.summary: Silicon-based battery electrodes hold more energy but lose charge-carrying ions during first use. The method tops up the positive electrode from an auxiliary electrode during activation so that both electrodes finish discharge at carefully set voltages, improving capacity and lifetime.

EP3294294.headline: Repurposed drug for high lung blood pressure
EP3294294.summary: Pulmonary hypertension, high blood pressure in the lungs' arteries, has limited treatments. The method administers an ascomycin, a class of compounds already known for other medical uses, to treat or prevent the condition.

EP3166049.headline: AI answers questions about pictures by looking closer
EP3166049.summary: Answering a question about an image requires focusing on the relevant part, which differs from question to question. A neural network reads the question, generates custom filters from its meaning and uses them to highlight the matching regions of the image while ignoring the rest, improving answers.

WO2016187352.headline: Smart glasses that warn of nearby dangers
WO2016187352.summary: Workers and others may not notice hazards around them. A head-mounted device with a transparent display and sensors compares readings against preset threat patterns and, when a threshold is crossed, shows a warning in the wearer's field of view.

WO2016187538.headline: Coated metal powders for better 3D printing
WO2016187538.summary: Metal 3D printing fuses powder particles together, which can leave weak spots. Each metal particle, 10 to 150 micrometres across, is coated with a second metal that melts at a lower temperature, helping particles bond more easily during printing.

EP3307282.headline: Engineered immune cells to fight cancer
EP3307282.summary: Immune cells can be engineered to carry receptors that seek out markers on cancer cells. These constructs, targeting markers such as Trop-2 or a chemical tag attached by a prior antibody, are given to patients with cancer or immune disorders, sometimes with a preliminary antibody dose to reduce side effects.

EP3307704.headline: Greener route to a key plastics ingredient
EP3307704.summary: Acrylic acid, used in paints, adhesives and nappies, is normally made from petroleum. Using modified zeolite catalysts, it can be produced from lactic acid and similar compounds, potentially from renewable sources, with acetaldehyde as the main by-product.

WO2016201218.headline: Restarting stalled synthetic fuel reactors
WO2016201218.summary: Reactors that convert synthesis gas into fuels or chemicals such as methane, methanol or dimethyl ether sometimes stop unexpectedly. A method is provided for restarting such processes safely, in conventional or compact microchannel reactors.

US10228983.headline: Smarter placement of software containers in clouds
US10228983.summary: Cloud applications run in containers inside virtual machines, and poor placement wastes resources. A management module monitors performance metrics to decide which virtual machine each container should run in, and keeps critical containers available if a machine fails.

WO2018028069.headline: In-car box scores how safely you drive
WO2018028069.summary: Insurers and fleet managers want objective measures of driving habits. A unit in the vehicle records location, acceleration and heading along with data from the car's computer, uploads it to a cloud server or phone, and the server analyses it to produce a safe-driving evaluation sent back to the driver.

EP3320659.headline: New radio signalling that copes with distortion
EP3320659.summary: Wireless signals are distorted by movement and reflections. Data is spread across time and frequency using a two-dimensional transform before being sent over many narrow channels, in a way compatible with existing 4G-style systems; the receiver reverses the process to map the distortions and recover clean data.

EP3319369.headline: Sensor networks route data via trusted neighbours
EP3319369.summary: Battery-powered sensor networks pass messages hop by hop, and poorly chosen hops drain nodes or expose data. Each node checks neighbours' remaining energy and trust scores, keeps only those above thresholds, ranks them and sends to the most trustworthy.

EP3323126.headline: Faster on-screen feedback for voice commands
EP3323126.summary: Cloud speech recognition is accurate but slow to respond. The device runs a smaller recogniser locally and shows provisional text on screen straight away, while audio is also sent to a server whose fuller results arrive later, making voice assistants feel more responsive.

EP3394069.headline: New chemistry step for making HIV drugs
EP3394069.summary: HIV integrase inhibitors are an important class of antiretroviral medicine. A new intermediate compound and a process for preparing it are provided, helping manufacture such drugs.

US9633282.headline: Teaching image AI with colour and depth
US9633282.summary: Image-recognising networks trained only on colour photos miss shape information. Starting from a colour-trained network, it is fine-tuned on depth images, copied, and then fine-tuned again on colour images, producing a network enriched with depth knowledge for better recognition.

EP3329464.headline: Copying animation features between different characters
EP3329464.summary: Animators spend much time reproducing facial expressions or movements on new characters. By placing marker points on a source and target character and mapping between them regardless of shape differences, attributes such as expressions can be transferred automatically.

WO2017021819.headline: Making proteins in bacteria more efficiently
WO2017021819.summary: Producing therapeutic peptides and proteins in bacteria can be inefficient. The process expresses a synthetic gene for the desired protein fused to ubiquitin in bacterial cells, aiding production.

US10298601.headline: Hiding a website's name inside its address
US10298601.summary: Secure web connections need the right digital certificate for the site requested. By encoding the host name into part of a long IPv6 network address, a server receiving a connection can read the host name from the address itself and present the correct certificate.

EP3341806.headline: Turning engineering drawings into control software
EP3341806.summary: Industrial plants are documented in diagrams that engineers must manually translate into control-system configurations. The method analyses each diagram symbol by its reference points and line directions, builds a graph of it, matches it against known engineering elements and records the best match and position in a file.

EP3341744.headline: Detecting failing units in power capacitor banks
EP3341744.summary: Capacitor banks in electricity grids contain many units, and a single failing unit is hard to find. A test signal is applied to the bank, its electrical response measured and compared with an earlier response, revealing whether any unit's impedance has drifted from normal.

WO2017039858.headline: 3D printers that check and correct themselves
WO2017039858.summary: 3D printed objects often deviate from their designs. During printing, 3D cameras measure the object in real time, compare the measurements with the expected ones from the design, identify discrepancies caused by errors, and compensate so the final object comes out right.

KR20170010547.headline: Spring keeps brake pads steady and quiet
KR20170010547.summary: Brake pads in disc brakes can rattle and wear unevenly. A specially shaped spring sits between the brake carrier and pad plates, gripping the carrier and supporting the pads so they slide smoothly while being held firmly.

CN106448465.headline: Rollable screen adjusts picture as it unrolls
CN106448465.summary: Flexible screens that roll around a spindle show varying amounts of display. A sensor on the spindle or housing measures how far the screen has been pulled out, and a controller resizes the image in real time to fit the visible area.

WO2017150032.headline: AI recognises what people are doing in video
WO2017150032.summary: Automatically identifying actions in video, for security or sport analysis, is difficult. The system tracks objects, follows pixel movements inside a box around each one, crops these trajectories and images into chunks, and feeds them to a recurrent neural network that scores each possible action.

EP3420700.headline: Safely simulating cyberattacks on live networks
EP3420700.summary: Security testing in a lab misses the quirks of a real company network. Controllers placed in each network zone take turns playing attacker and target, running simulated malicious traffic through actual switches and routers, while a central planner analyses the results to assess overall security.

WO2017047078.headline: Game map shows where sounds come from
WO2017047078.summary: Players in virtual worlds can struggle to locate sounds. The game detects where a sound originates near the player's character and marks that spot on a simplified mini-map on screen, helping players react.

EP3352928.headline: Making biofuel from cheap raw materials
EP3352928.summary: Biofuel production often needs specific feedstocks. In this system a feed is pressurised and heated, reformed into a slurry, solids are removed, and the mixture cooled, depressurised and separated to yield biofuel from diverse, inexpensive starting materials.

EP3430556.headline: Catching malware that hides inside trusted programs
EP3430556.summary: Some malware starts a legitimate program and then hollows it out, replacing its code so it looks trustworthy. The method watches each new process's calls to the operating system, checks for those known to rewrite executable memory or entry points, and applies security policies when hollowing is detected.

EP3356003.headline: Games that adapt to your heart rate
EP3356003.summary: Virtual reality experiences can be too intense or too tame. Sensors measure physical signs such as heart rate and send them to the console, which adjusts the game, for example lowering difficulty or scariness when the player's pulse rises.

EP3359439.headline: Self-driving cars that steer like their owner
EP3359439.summary: Automated steering can feel unnatural. While the driver steers manually, sensors record steering angle and the positions of nearby objects; deep learning builds a model of that driving style, which the car then applies when steering itself.

EP3430513.headline: Several voice assistants working together
EP3430513.summary: Different apps have their own voice assistants that do not cooperate. This system lets specialist assistants register with a general one and listen for relevant requests; when the general assistant hears a matching intent, it hands control to the specialist, expanding what it can handle.

KR20170029956.headline: Cheaper way to wind electric motor coils
KR20170029956.summary: Winding stator coils for vehicle motors is complex and costly. Straightened wire pieces are cut, slipped into insulated slots in the stator core and their exposed ends twisted in opposite directions and overlapped, simplifying manufacture and reducing cost.

EP3433816.headline: Blending adverts seamlessly into videos and images
EP3433816.summary: Inserted adverts often look jarring. The system takes a source piece of content, finds a suitable region in a target video or image, and integrates the source there so it looks natural and unobtrusive, for advertising, entertainment or communication.

JP6112527.headline: Memory-saving bonus logic for slot machines
JP6112527.summary: Pachislot machines must decide when to enter a bonus phase within strict memory limits on the control board. The machine checks a few status flags and, if conditions are met, runs a lottery whose outcome determines the switch, using the same winning combinations across game states to save memory.

JP2017202193.headline: Clearer bonus-mode indicator on slot machines
JP2017202193.summary: Players may miss when a slot machine enters a bonus phase. One segment of the existing credit-count display doubles as a bonus indicator, lighting from the next game until the player settles their credits.

EP3332509.headline: Creating custom virtual networks on demand
EP3332509.summary: 5G networks are divided into slices tailored to different services. An orchestrator receives requests to create, modify or terminate a slice, adds services, prepares a descriptor and instructs a resource orchestrator to set up or tear down the required virtual network functions.

WO2017082947.headline: Bundling network links for data-centre storage
WO2017082947.summary: Storage networks running Fibre Channel over Ethernet need reliable, high-capacity connections. Multiple physical links between an edge device and a switch are combined into one logical link through an aggregation layer, increasing throughput and resilience.

EP3681197.headline: Phones save battery by not scanning everything
EP3681197.summary: Idle phones constantly measure signals from many directions, draining power. The phone checks resources such as beams one at a time and stops as soon as one meets a quality threshold, switching off its receiver. It also handles 5G signals formatted in different ways across time slots.

EP3840464.headline: Connecting phones to virtual 5G networks
EP3840464.summary: 5G networks run as virtual slices tailored to different services. The phone first connects to an underlying network, which assigns it to a slice; procedures allow either the phone or the network to request a new slice, change the phone's profile or switch slices.

EP3411660.headline: Sharing one laser among several lidar sensors
EP3411660.summary: Self-driving cars and robots use lidar, which bounces laser pulses off surroundings to map them in 3D. Instead of giving every sensor its own laser, a single central laser feeds several sensor heads through fibre-optic cables. The laser produces very short, clean pulses, which keeps the system compact and lowers cost.

EP3464512.headline: Turning plant waste into liquid fuel
