EP3464512.summary: Wood, crop residues and other biomass can be converted into petrol- and diesel-like liquids, offering an alternative to fossil fuels. The feedstock is heated with hydrogen over a catalyst, the char is removed, and the vapours are refined in a second step to strip out oxygen. A particular way of making the catalysts improves the process.

EP3920459.headline: Building blocks for faster 5G mobile networks
EP3920459.summary: Mobile networks must serve very different needs at once, from streaming video to tiny sensor messages. Phones and base stations can be told how to transmit using short codes, mix different radio signal formats in consecutive time slots and handle some data streams with error-correction and others without. This flexibility underpins fifth-generation (5G) networks.

EP3452101.headline: Messenger RNA that makes the body produce medicines
EP3452101.summary: Rather than injecting a therapeutic protein directly, patients can be given RNA, the genetic instructions that tell cells to make the protein themselves. The RNA is designed so that cells produce more of the protein, which is useful in gene therapy. Kits and formulations for delivering it are also covered.

WO2017106821.headline: Low-energy sensing of when current stops
WO2017106821.summary: Power supplies in phones and other devices switch currents on and off thousands of times a second, and need to know the instant a current falls to zero to switch efficiently. A simple circuit compares two voltages to spot that moment and then flips the switches, using very little power itself.

WO2017211367.headline: Wind turbines that learn their best settings
WO2017211367.summary: A wind turbine's output depends on how its blades are angled and how fast the rotor spins, and factory settings are not always ideal for a specific site or as the machine ages. The controller tries slightly different settings for a period, compares the electricity produced with the original settings, and adopts whichever yields more.

JP2018000796.headline: Clearer bonus-round limits on slot machines
JP2018000796.summary: Gambling rules cap how long a slot machine's bonus period can run, at 1,500 games. When a player earns extra bonus games that would push past this cap, the machine shows a celebratory message instead of a game count, so players are not misled into thinking they can keep playing beyond the limit.

WO2017106998.headline: Sharpening blurry images with added detail
WO2017106998.summary: Low-resolution photos look blurry when enlarged. The method first filters the image to pick out its important features, enlarges that feature map, and then rebuilds a new, larger image from it, producing sharper results than simple stretching. It can be used wherever small images need to be displayed or analysed at higher quality.

WO2017120279.headline: Mixed powders for stronger 3D-printed parts
WO2017120279.summary: In laser 3D printing, objects are built layer by layer from powder that a laser melts together. Using a powder blend of two different materials, where the laser only needs to melt one of them to bind the layer, opens up new material combinations and properties for printed parts.

WO2017118940.headline: New solid forms of a cancer drug
WO2017118940.summary: Selinexor is a medicine used against certain blood cancers. The same drug molecule can exist in different crystalline or non-crystalline solid forms, which affect how stable it is and how well it dissolves. New forms and ways of making them are described, along with pills or other formulations containing them.

EP3479305.headline: Smart home devices that cooperate without the cloud
EP3479305.summary: Connected gadgets usually send everything to a company's servers, which is costly and raises privacy worries. Here devices talk directly to one another, store information among themselves and each run their own learning software to spot patterns in how people use them, so the group can anticipate what a user wants without a central server.

EP3408800.headline: Teaching AI systems by describing lessons
EP3408800.summary: Building a machine-learning model normally needs specialist programming. Here a developer writes, in a purpose-built teaching language, what concepts the system should learn and in what order. An 'architect' component then proposes a suitable model, and the engine trains it lesson by lesson, lowering the skill barrier to creating AI applications.

WO2017126270.headline: Sturdier battery packs with glued-in cells
WO2017126270.summary: Battery packs for cars and other machines bundle many cells inside a case, and loose or misaligned cells cause faults. Each cell is glued at the top to a holder and at the bottom to the case, which fixes it firmly and lines up its terminals accurately, making the pack more reliable and simpler to assemble.

WO2018044482.headline: Cutting chip power use during factory testing
WO2018044482.summary: Before shipping, microchips are tested by running many parts at once, which can draw so much power that voltages sag and tests fail. Instead of adding test switches everywhere, only a chosen few of the chip's existing clock-control circuits are reused to switch off sections during tests, saving power and chip space.

WO2018052538.headline: Warning smart devices about unreliable power
WO2018052538.summary: After a blackout, power may return only briefly before failing again, which can damage or confuse connected appliances. A smart electricity meter estimates how reliable the restored supply is likely to be and passes that forecast to household devices, so they can decide whether to restart immediately or wait.

EP3264225.headline: Saving battery by processing sensor data locally
EP3264225.summary: Devices with many sensors drain their batteries sending everything to the cloud. The device judges how critical its surroundings are, checks its remaining energy, processing power and network bandwidth, and then uses a set of priority rules to decide which sensor data to process on the device itself, stretching battery life.

US9761294.headline: Memory chips that avoid writing to hot spots
US9761294.summary: Computer memory can become unreliable or wear out faster when parts of it overheat. Before storing data at a given address, the system checks the temperature there and only writes if it is below a safety threshold, improving reliability of servers and other hardware.

EP3293691.headline: Shopping suggestions triggered by your mood
EP3293691.summary: A phone or similar device detects when its owner's emotional state changes, for example from calm to stressed. It then looks up content tagged with that new mood, and, taking the user's location into account, launches an app recommending a related product or service. The aim is advertising and recommendations that respond to how people feel.

WO2018045063.headline: Natural bacteria that protect crops from worms
WO2018045063.summary: Microscopic soil worms called nematodes damage crop roots and cut yields. A treatment combining two naturally occurring soil bacteria is applied to seeds or into the furrow at planting, suppressing the worms and offering farmers an alternative to chemical pesticides.

US9774478.headline: Keeping parallel data lanes in step
US9774478.summary: Fast data links split traffic across several parallel channels, but tiny timing differences between them can corrupt the combined stream. Special buffers measure how far each lane is out of step and nudge the data or clock by whole bits to realign them, keeping the lanes synchronised with minimal delay.

EP3300238.headline: More efficient converters for direct-current power
EP3300238.summary: Many power systems, such as data centres and renewable installations, need to change one direct-current voltage into another. A converter using a resonant circuit and transformer, with its switches run at the circuit's natural frequency, achieves this with low losses while a controller holds the output voltage at the desired level.

EP3433990.headline: Automatic security for short-lived cloud servers
EP3433990.summary: Cloud computing spins up temporary virtual machines for minutes or hours, often too quickly for conventional security set-up. A security system watches for new instances, reads their configuration and installed software, and automatically generates and applies a tailored security policy before they can be exploited.

WO2018053340.headline: Using duelling neural networks to sharpen images
WO2018053340.summary: Enlarging a small picture usually produces a blurry result. Here two artificial neural networks are trained against each other: one invents sharp high-resolution versions of low-resolution images, while the other tries to tell these fakes from real photographs. The competition pushes the first network to produce convincingly detailed images.

EP3437002.headline: Contracts that execute themselves from live data
EP3437002.summary: Legal contracts are usually static documents that people must monitor and enforce. Here contracts are built from programmable clauses alongside ordinary legal text, connected to data feeds and blockchain ledgers, so terms such as payments or penalties can be triggered automatically when real-world conditions are met.

EP3676172.headline: Quieter aircraft wing slats on approach
EP3676172.summary: The movable slats on the front of aircraft wings generate noise when extended for take-off and landing. A flexible shield built into the slat's lower edge stays flat when the slat is retracted and curves outward automatically when it is deployed, smoothing the airflow and reducing noise around airports.

EP3520368.headline: Tamper-proof software updates recorded on a blockchain
EP3520368.summary: Devices receive many software updates, and recovering from a failed or incompatible one can be messy. Each configuration of a device's software is recorded on a blockchain-style distributed ledger; when an update cannot be applied to the current version, the system fetches a compatible version and logs that too, giving a trustworthy history to recover from.

WO2017189497.headline: Faster combining of data streams in chips
WO2017189497.summary: Chips often need to merge several slower data streams into one high-speed stream for transmission. Using four timing signals offset from one another, the data is routed through registers and switches in a pattern that combines the streams efficiently and with less timing error.

EP3301542.headline: Chips that slow down briefly when voltage dips
EP3301542.summary: Sudden drops in a chip's supply voltage can cause calculation errors or crashes. A monitoring circuit detects the dip and briefly stretches the current clock cycle, giving the circuitry extra time to finish its work safely before the next tick, which avoids having to run the chip permanently slower.

US10003521.headline: Shortcut for storage traffic between servers
US10003521.summary: In data-centre storage networks, traffic between a server and its storage often passes through a central switch even when both are plugged into the same gateway. The gateway recognises such pairs and routes their traffic directly between them, bypassing the switch to cut delay and congestion.

EP3316198.headline: Smarter performance dashboards for facilities management
EP3316198.summary: Companies running many buildings struggle to track whether operations are meeting their goals. The system pulls together operational data, derives key performance indicators and thresholds, adjusts for factors that make sites hard to compare, and refines the indicators and visual dashboards based on how managers actually use them.

EP3455219.headline: Molecules that mark disease proteins for destruction
EP3455219.summary: Many diseases involve proteins that are hard to block with conventional drugs. These compounds act as molecular tags that hijack the cell's own waste-disposal machinery to break down a chosen protein entirely. The approach is aimed at new treatments where the target protein can be removed rather than merely inhibited.

WO2017200660.headline: Skipping wasted work in graphics rendering
WO2017200660.summary: Graphics chips often draw a scene in tiles, re-running the same drawing commands for each tile even when many shapes are not visible in it. A conditional jump inserted into the command list lets the chip skip commands for shapes that pre-processing has flagged as irrelevant, saving time and power in games and other graphics.

EP3458445.headline: Drugs targeting a common cancer mutation
EP3458445.summary: A mutated form of the KRAS protein, called G12C, drives many lung, bowel and pancreatic cancers and was long considered impossible to drug. These compounds bind permanently to the mutant protein and switch it off, and are intended for use in cancer medicines.

US10110154.headline: Safer shutdown of electric motors in a fault
US10110154.summary: When an electric vehicle's motor drive develops a fault, it must be put into a safe state without damaging the battery or motor. The controller switches between two safe modes, short-circuit and freewheeling, according to measured conditions, and slows the motor if its windings overheat, protecting the system until it can be repaired.

EP4194887.headline: Lidar that looks harder where nothing is seen
EP4194887.summary: Lidar sensors map surroundings by timing reflected laser light, and self-driving cars need to see far ahead. When one part of the field of view shows a nearby object but another part shows nothing, the system sends more light into the empty region to look further out, detecting more distant objects there.

EP3465412.headline: Automatically building websites for small businesses
EP3465412.summary: Small firms often lack the time or skill to design a website. Based on answers to a questionnaire and information gathered about the business online, the system generates text and images, matches them to layouts and design kits suited to that type of business, and produces a complete site the owner can then edit visually.

EP3542557.headline: Picking the right gateway for low-power sensors
EP3542557.summary: Battery-powered sensors on long-range, low-power networks may be heard by several gateways at once. When a device asks to join, the network chooses one gateway, based on policy and on what application the device runs, and can assign a nearby 'edge' server to handle its data locally for faster response.

WO2017212757.headline: Diagnosing faults in solar panel strings
WO2017212757.summary: Solar installations connect many panels in long strings, and a fault in one is hard to locate. By measuring the string's electrical impedance at different frequencies and calculating its inductance from a circuit model, the device can tell whether and where the string is faulty without dismantling it.

US10126984.headline: Faster look-ups in deduplicated storage
US10126984.summary: Storage systems that eliminate duplicate copies of data rely on large indexes of metadata, too big to keep entirely in fast memory. By watching which data is requested when and where, the system moves the most relevant metadata into fast memory and adapts as usage patterns shift, speeding up reads.

WO2019017991.headline: Smarter estimates of electric-car battery charge
WO2019017991.summary: Drivers need accurate readings of how much charge remains in a battery, but voltage and temperature readings alone can mislead. A learning model that also takes into account how the specific vehicle is used predicts the battery's state in real time, giving more trustworthy range estimates.

WO2018004614.headline: Stretchy fabric patch that monitors the heart
WO2018004614.summary: Wearable health monitors are often rigid and uncomfortable. A soft, stretchable patch built onto fabric carries wiggly metal tracks and sensors, including heart-monitoring electrodes and a stretch sensor, so it can move with the body while recording biological signals.

EP3488352.headline: One set of sockets, several connection standards
EP3488352.summary: Computer processors talk to accelerators and other components over different connection standards, each usually needing its own dedicated sockets. Here one shared set of connectors can be configured so that some carry one protocol and others another, giving system builders more flexibility and reducing wasted hardware.

US11030176.headline: Spreading file descriptions across many servers
US11030176.summary: Large files such as videos or images come with descriptive information that must be found quickly. The system stores these descriptions across many storage servers, with a coordination layer that remembers which server holds what, so requests can be answered rapidly even at very large scale.

EP3602556.headline: Stopping charge leaks in memory chips
EP3602556.summary: Writing data into memory cells sometimes uses a brief negative voltage boost to make the write reliable, but the boosted charge can leak away through the writing circuitry. Letting part of the circuit's ground connection float during the boost chokes off that leak, making writes more dependable at low power.

WO2018013094.headline: Compact electric vehicle with fold-away handlebar
WO2018013094.summary: A small electric vehicle has a cover hinged to its body and a control bar hinged to the cover. Folding the cover down onto the body tucks the bar between them, making the vehicle compact for storage or carrying.

EP3728133.headline: Adding aluminium to boost battery capacity
EP3728133.summary: Lithium-rich battery electrode materials promise high capacity but tend to release gas during charging, which is a safety and durability problem. Including aluminium in the material suppresses this gas formation and increases how much charge the electrode can hold.

EP3563545.headline: Blockchain security for networks of connected devices
EP3563545.summary: Networks of connected sensors and gadgets are vulnerable because devices are hard to trust and manage. A collection of techniques uses blockchain-style ledgers, trusted hardware environments and policy engines so devices can securely join a network, prove their identity, share resources and recover if a component fails.

EP3497962.headline: Managing radio congestion between connected cars
EP3497962.summary: Cars that broadcast warnings to one another share a limited radio channel that can become congested. Each vehicle measures how busy the channel is, both by energy levels and by decoding other transmissions, and adjusts its own power and transmission settings, taking other wireless technologies on the channel into account.

US10528864.headline: Faster AI chips that skip zeros
US10528864.summary: Neural networks involve huge numbers of multiplications, many of which involve zeros and so contribute nothing. This accelerator stores only the non-zero values together with their positions, multiplies just those, and routes the results to the right accumulators, saving time and energy in AI hardware.

WO2018141918.headline: Washer-dryer that uses space inside its door
WO2018141918.summary: Combined washer-dryers have limited drum space. The machine's door has a domed rear wall that bulges into the drum and is sealed to the front wall, creating a usable cavity inside the door itself.

EP4134112.headline: Auto-injector pen that cannot fire by accident
EP4134112.summary: Self-injection pens must not trigger when dropped or handled carelessly. Inside the two-part casing, a sliding lock engages the inner sleeve to stop it moving until the device is readied, after which the lock releases and the injection can proceed, improving safety for patients injecting themselves.

WO2018160383.headline: Cleaner data writes in low-power memory
WO2018160383.summary: Memory chips sometimes use a brief negative voltage boost to write data reliably, but the boost charge can leak away. Two capacitors apply the boost separately to the two stages of the writing circuit, reducing leakage and making low-power writes more dependable.

EP3533539.headline: 3D-printing jet engine blades from two steels
EP3533539.summary: Compressor blades in gas turbines need different properties in different places. Using laser-based 3D printing, a single component is built from two different iron-based alloys in different regions, with a specific chromium, nickel and cobalt mix that avoids a weakening phase forming and improves mechanical performance.

EP3513288.headline: Squeezing more work out of computing clusters
EP3513288.summary: Large computing clusters often sit partly idle because jobs reserve more capacity than they actually use. The scheduler watches real usage, places extra opportunistic work on under-used machines, and pulls it back if the machines become overloaded, improving throughput without harming the regular jobs.

EP3515443.headline: Drug combination for hard-to-treat cancers
EP3515443.summary: Drugs that cut off a tumour's blood supply fail against some cancers, such as colorectal and ovarian. Combining such a drug with a topoisomerase inhibitor, another class of chemotherapy, stops cancer cells multiplying and triggers their death in these cases.

CN107893309.headline: Washing machine that looks at your laundry
CN107893309.summary: Choosing the right wash cycle is guesswork for many users. A camera inside the washing machine photographs the load, software works out the fabric type and quantity, and together with a reading of the water quality the machine adjusts the washing programme automatically.

EP3385840.headline: Sharing a graphics chip fairly among virtual machines
EP3385840.summary: When several virtual machines share one graphics processor, they compete for its fast on-chip memory. Hardware allocates separate portions of this memory to each virtual machine or application and reserves space in main memory to catch any overflow, keeping cloud graphics workloads from interfering with each other.

US10360191.headline: Penalising unreliable voters in a blockchain
US10360191.summary: Blockchains rely on many computers voting on whether transactions are valid, and some may vote dishonestly or carelessly. The system keeps a tally of how often each validator disagrees with the final consensus and, once a threshold is passed, proposes sanctions against it, strengthening trust in the network.

US10439890.headline: Spreading computing tasks across nearby devices
US10439890.summary: Connected sensors and gadgets can share computing work among themselves rather than sending it all to distant data centres. A coordinating node assesses each nearby device's capabilities and uses an optimisation model, accounting for battery wear, signal loss and differing processing power, to decide which device does which part of the task.

US10452377.headline: Rehearsing software upgrades before going live
US10452377.summary: Upgrading business IT systems is risky, since failures can take down live operations. The simulator takes an inventory of the real system, builds a scaled-down replica with equivalent hardware configuration, runs the upgrade on the replica and evaluates the result, so problems appear before the real upgrade.

EP3607732.headline: Safely routing cloud apps through a company gateway
EP3607732.summary: Companies want visibility and control over staff use of cloud software without disrupting it. A gateway sits between users and the cloud application, rewriting web addresses so traffic passes through the gateway transparently, where it can be inspected and protected.

CN108017445.headline: Microbial treatment for salty, alkaline soils
CN108017445.summary: Salt-affected and alkaline soils are unproductive for farming. A soil treatment combines a beneficial Bacillus bacterium with industrial by-products such as phosphate tailings, phosphogypsum, sugar-mill waste and seaweed residue. Applied at 30 to 80 kg per unit of land, it improves fertiliser uptake, crop yield and soil quality.

WO2018089110.headline: Tracking objects in video more accurately
WO2018089110.summary: Computer vision systems that spot objects in video can lose them or produce false detections between frames. Combining what was tracked in the previous frame with fresh detections in the current frame yields a small set of likely object positions, and the system shows the result to the user, for example in surveillance or driver-assistance.

US10127722.headline: Virtual tours mixing 3D models and photos
US10127722.summary: Property tours and similar visualisations can use either 3D models, which may look artificial, or photos, which are fixed. As a user moves a virtual camera through a 3D model of a space captured on a mobile device, the system picks the real photo whose position and angle best match the new viewpoint, blending realism with free navigation.

EP3869416.headline: AI photo captions that look where it matters
EP3869416.summary: Automatic captioning of photos needs to decide which part of the image each word refers to. The system weighs attention across regions of the image for each word and also learns when to rely on language context rather than the picture, for example for words like 'the'. This produces more accurate and natural descriptions.

EP3399466.headline: Generating training images to spot equipment damage
EP3399466.summary: Teaching software to recognise damage on industrial equipment requires many labelled example images, which are expensive to create. A user marks areas on a mask that is combined with an unlabelled photo to produce labelled training images, which train the recognition system or generate further training images for it.

EP3548005.headline: Natural cell packages to deliver drugs
EP3548005.summary: Exosomes are tiny bubbles that cells naturally release to carry material between them. Loading them with a medicine turns them into delivery vehicles that can be targeted to a particular tissue or organ, with potential uses against cancer, inflammatory, infectious, allergic and autoimmune diseases.

WO2018106971.headline: Recognising who is speaking with neural networks
WO2018106971.summary: Identifying a speaker from their voice is useful for security and personalised services. The system extracts the parts of a recording containing speech, computes characteristic features of each snippet, scores them with a trained model, and combines the scores to decide who is talking.

EP3631368.headline: Showing passengers what their self-driving car cannot see
EP3631368.summary: Self-driving cars rely on sensors with limited range and field of view, and passengers cannot tell where coverage is weak. Using the planned route and sensor data, the system predicts blind spots along the way and overlays them on an augmented-reality display, helping occupants understand and trust the vehicle.

EP3630778.headline: Compounds that unblock the immune system
EP3630778.summary: The enzyme MAP4K1, also known as HPK1, dampens immune responses and is linked to cancer and inflammatory, neurological and heart conditions. These newly designed compounds block the enzyme and are intended for medicines treating such diseases.

US10594484.headline: Sharing only the identity details you choose
US10594484.summary: Proving your age or address online often means handing over far more personal data than needed. A digital identity service lets a person pick which stored attributes to share, issues a unique one-off token, and reveals only those attributes when a business presents the token back to the service.

EP3560111.headline: Antenna and radio designs for 5G devices
EP3560111.summary: Very high-frequency 'millimetre wave' radio promises fast 5G connections but is hard to build into compact devices. A collection of designs covers combined antennas, scalable phased-array transceivers, sending radio signals over a single cable, reducing clock noise and modular chip arrangements for receivers.

WO2019231466.headline: Scoring how well buildings perform for a business
WO2019231466.summary: Organisations running many sites struggle to judge which are operating effectively. The platform gathers sensor and other data from each site, sets benchmark values for chosen economic factors, compares actual performance with the benchmarks, and displays effectiveness scores for each location.

EP4398113.headline: Letting processors hand work to specialist chips
EP4398113.summary: Modern computers pair general-purpose processors with specialised accelerators for tasks like graphics or AI. A dedicated instruction marks the start of a block of code to be offloaded to an accelerator, so the processor can hand that work over cleanly and efficiently.

EP3563595.headline: Relaying phone signals to avoid radio collisions
EP3563595.summary: A device such as a phone may be too far from a base station to reach it directly, so another device relays its transmission. The relay adds a preamble in a different signal format before forwarding, which warns other users of the channel and protects the relayed data from collisions.

EP3583485.headline: Smart assistant that recognises who is present
EP3583485.summary: Voice assistants with cameras and sensors could personalise their behaviour, but constantly analysing everyone is computationally costly. The device spends few resources tracking people it already recognises, more on unknown people when a known user is present, and most when an unknown person is present with no known user around.

US10360517.headline: Automatically tuning machine-learning models in parallel
US10360517.summary: Machine-learning models have settings, called hyperparameters, that greatly affect performance but are tedious to choose by hand. The system runs many training sessions at once, each with a different configuration chosen by a search strategy, scores each on validation data and picks the best, speeding up model development.

EP3589990.headline: More accurate distance readings for lidar
EP3589990.summary: Lidar sensors measure distance by timing laser reflections, but reflections vary with surface shape and reflectivity. Comparing the returning signal against several expected patterns identifies the best match, yielding better range estimates and information about the surface. Coded and staggered pulses and on-chip processing further improve accuracy.

EP3666032.headline: Phones using mobile and Wi-Fi networks at once
EP3666032.summary: A phone normally sends a given data session over either the mobile network or Wi-Fi. Here the device registers with both and requests a single session that can send data over both at the same time, allowing traffic to be steered or switched between them for better speed and reliability.

WO2018176000.headline: Fake sensor data to train self-driving systems
WO2018176000.summary: Autonomous vehicles learn from vast quantities of sensor recordings, but rare or dangerous situations are hard to capture. The system generates synthetic sensor data by modifying real recordings or simulating virtual environments, letting the control software train on scenarios that real data lacks and learn to ignore unwanted artefacts.

US10089144.headline: Scheduling computing jobs by predicting demand
US10089144.summary: Shared computing platforms can miss deadlines when jobs compete for resources. By measuring how past jobs used resources, the system builds a predictive model, estimates whether upcoming jobs will finish on time, assigns them reward values accordingly, and reschedules them to make the best use of capacity.

EP3602384.headline: Redacting personal details from documents in stages
EP3602384.summary: Documents often contain names, addresses and other personal information that must be masked before sharing. Text passes through successive layers, including pattern matching, lookup tables and machine learning, each estimating how likely a word is to be personal data and masking it when confident, otherwise passing it to the next layer.

EP3612942.headline: Stopping big data transfers blocking small ones
EP3612942.summary: Computers move blocks of data between memory locations without troubling the main processor, using queues of transfer requests. Very large blocks can hold up smaller ones. Splitting big transfers into fragments ensures small requests are processed promptly, improving responsiveness.

EP3636333.headline: Twistable moisture trap for battery casings
EP3636333.summary: Electric-vehicle battery housings need protection from humidity. A small dryer cartridge holding moisture-absorbing material has a cover that rotates relative to its housing: in one position the openings line up to let air through, in another they are blocked, so the desiccant can be sealed off until needed.

WO2019051507.headline: Spotting ransomware by how it behaves
WO2019051507.summary: Ransomware encrypts victims' files and demands payment, and new variants evade signature-based antivirus. A security engine watches programs for tell-tale behaviours such as encrypting files or disabling backups, provisionally classifies them, protects system resources, and raises or lowers a threat score as it observes further actions, acting when a threshold is crossed.

EP3695615.headline: Plugging outside services into cloud document platforms
EP3695615.summary: Businesses storing files on a cloud collaboration platform often want to process them with specialised external tools. An integration layer detects events such as uploads, applies rules to choose among external services hosted elsewhere, sends the content for processing and feeds the results back into the platform.

WO2019075045.headline: New drug molecules blocking galectin-3
WO2019075045.summary: Galectin-3 is a protein implicated in fibrosis, inflammation and cancer. A new family of small-molecule compounds inhibits it, with formulations and methods for making and using them for potential medicines.

EP3622371.headline: Self-calibrating cameras on VR headsets
EP3622371.summary: Mixed-reality headsets use paired cameras to track handheld controllers, and the cameras drift out of alignment over time. By detecting the controller's light sources in each camera's view and working out its position from each, the headset can calibrate the cameras against each other without special equipment.

US10718425.headline: Better lubrication for automatic gearbox brakes
US10718425.summary: Automatic transmissions use friction brakes made of stacked plates that must be kept oiled to avoid wear and overheating. Oil flows through a passage in the fixed holder into a ring-shaped chamber and out through holes directly onto the rotating and fixed plates, improving lubrication.

EP3701037.headline: Cutting lactic acid losses in ethanol fermentation
EP3701037.summary: Bacterial contamination in biofuel fermentation produces lactic acid, which lowers ethanol yields. Adding a particular enzyme, a lytic polysaccharide monooxygenase, before or during the sugar-release and fermentation stages reduces or prevents the build-up of lactic acid.

WO2019089646.headline: Risk testing tool for blockchain systems
WO2019089646.summary: Organisations adopting blockchain systems lack standard ways to check they are working safely. A risk framework lets users choose which risks matter to them through a graphical interface and converts those choices into continuous, real-time validation tests run against the blockchain.

US10142129.headline: Stopping duplicate broadcast traffic in virtual networks
US10142129.summary: Data-centre networks that stretch virtual networks across sites can accidentally deliver the same broadcast packet twice when a device is connected through more than one network edge. Filtering techniques detect and drop these duplicates, keeping the overlay network efficient.

US10148493.headline: Translating network rules for public clouds
US10148493.summary: Companies moving to public cloud need their network policies and settings to carry over. A gateway receives requests in the cloud provider's own interface or an extended version, extracts and adds details such as device addresses, translates them into the native cloud format and forwards them, bridging in-house network management and cloud services.

EP4418392.headline: Stronger welds inside battery packs
EP4418392.summary: Battery packs join each cell's terminal to a current conductor by welding, and poor welds cause failures. Each joint uses a single spiral weld or at least two parallel straight welds of uniform width that never cross themselves or each other, giving consistent, reliable connections.

EP3506095.headline: Faster teamwork between computers training AI
EP3506095.summary: Training large neural networks is spread across many computers that must constantly exchange results, and this communication becomes a bottleneck. A software library groups the worker machines according to the pattern of messages they need to exchange, cutting the time spent communicating.

WO2018226150.headline: Compounds that unleash the immune system on cancer
WO2018226150.summary: The enzyme MALT1 helps regulate immune signalling. New compounds that potently block it are intended for immunotherapy approaches to cancer, especially bladder, colon, liver and lung cancers.

EP3539728.headline: Detecting robot faults by predicting their next move
EP3539728.summary: In factories with many robots, actuation faults can go unnoticed until they cause damage. A deep-learning model learns the normal sequence of robot activities and predicts what each robot should do next; when actual behaviour diverges from the prediction, a fault is flagged quickly and accurately.

EP3707572.headline: Computing platform for safe self-driving vehicles
EP3707572.summary: Driving a car autonomously means processing floods of data from cameras, radar, lidar and maps in real time. An energy-efficient system-on-a-chip and software architecture combine computer vision and established driver-assistance techniques with built-in redundancy to meet safety standards, scalable to cars, trucks, buses and even boats and aircraft.

WO2019014639.headline: Interior design challenges judged by the community
WO2019014639.summary: An app presents users with a room scene marked with spots to furnish. Players choose furniture items, some already owned and some not, to fill the marked spots, and once complete submit their design for other users to vote on. It combines a game with shopping for home furnishings.

EP3823245.headline: Network switches that speak several protocols
EP3823245.summary: Data-centre networks increasingly mix different low-level communication standards. Switch circuitry handles multiple such protocols on the same physical infrastructure and reports telemetry about its own operation, simplifying network design and monitoring.

WO2019133052.headline: Privacy-aware scheduling of camera analytics
WO2019133052.summary: Analysing video from many cameras, for instance in cities or vehicles, means deciding which device processes which task, while respecting privacy. The system maps the tasks and the connections between devices, checks each device's privacy level against the applicable policy, and schedules the work so that sensitive processing only happens where permitted.

EP3743430.headline: New compounds against inflammation and cell death
EP3743430.summary: RIPK1 is an enzyme involved in a form of cell death and in inflammation. A new chemical family modulates this enzyme and is proposed for treating conditions involving tissue necrosis or inflammation, among others.

EP3743451.headline: Better carbon for supercapacitor electrodes
EP3743451.summary: Ultracapacitors store and release electrical energy very rapidly, and their performance depends heavily on the carbon in their electrodes. New compositions and manufacturing methods produce carbon materials with improved electrochemical properties for use in such devices.

EP3676708.headline: Spotting what phase a computer workload is in
EP3676708.summary: Data-centre servers run many jobs whose demands on processing, memory and storage shift over time. A built-in monitor reads performance figures as a job runs, matches them against a table of known usage patterns and builds a running 'fingerprint' of the job, helping operators allocate resources more efficiently.

EP4312420.headline: Sharing cyber-attack warnings across many organisations
EP4312420.summary: Cyber attacks are often spotted first in one organisation while others remain exposed. This security system learns what normal network behaviour looks like, flags unusual activity that may signal a breach, and then sends 'inoculation' warnings to other devices or organisations so they can defend themselves before being hit.

EP3676254.headline: New drug compounds to fight cancer and viruses
EP3676254.summary: The body's immune system uses signalling proteins called interferons to fight tumours and infections. These chemical compounds block an enzyme (ENPP-1) that dampens interferon production, boosting the immune response. They are intended as medicines for treating cancer or viral infections.

US10931108.headline: Timing household chores to cut electricity costs
US10931108.summary: Running appliances such as washing machines at peak times is costly for households and strains the grid. Smart homes record when flexible chores could acceptably start, and the grid operator uses this across many homes to schedule them when power is cheaper and more plentiful, smoothing demand and lowering bills.

EP3758777.headline: Easier locking of syringes into medical injectors
EP3758777.summary: Powered injectors used in hospitals, for example to deliver contrast dye before scans, must grip the syringe plunger securely. A rotating sleeve inside the piston head pushes small pins outward to lock onto the plunger and retracts them to release it, making syringe changes quicker and more reliable.

EP3543343.headline: Cheaper ethanol from crop waste and wood
EP3543343.summary: Making fuel ethanol from straw, wood and other plant waste is held back by the cost of enzymes and long processing times. By reordering the steps so that some sugars are fermented before the main enzyme treatment and others after it, the process uses fewer enzymes, runs faster and yields more ethanol.

US11853436.headline: Stopping thieves from copying AI models
US11853436.summary: Companies that offer AI services online risk rivals reverse-engineering their models by repeatedly querying them and studying the answers. This technique adds small deliberate distortions to the confidence scores the model returns, so the final classification stays correct but the underlying model is much harder to copy.

US10734615.headline: Battery cells that unstick under ultraviolet light
US10734615.summary: Battery packs in consumer devices glue cells to a liner, which makes repair and recycling difficult. Here the adhesive holds firmly during normal use but weakens when exposed to ultraviolet light, so cells can be released cleanly when the pack is disassembled.

EP3688581.headline: Firmware updates that check their own compatibility
EP3688581.summary: Devices contain many pieces of low-level software (firmware) that must work together, and updating one can break another. Each firmware component carries a description of which versions of other components it depends on, letting the device check compatibility automatically before installing an update.

WO2019064214.headline: Purer building block for a diabetes drug
WO2019064214.summary: Linagliptin is a widely used medicine for type 2 diabetes. New crystalline forms of a key intermediate chemical, and methods for making them, aim to make manufacturing the drug more consistent and efficient.

CN109638214.headline: Stronger electrical joints inside battery packs
CN109638214.summary: In electric-vehicle battery modules, metal busbars are welded to cell terminals, and the weld alone limits how much current can flow. Adding a separate conductive piece alongside the weld creates a second current path, greatly increasing carrying capacity and reducing heating.

WO2019079530.headline: Several self-driving brains vote on each manoeuvre
WO2019079530.summary: Relying on a single decision-making system in a self-driving car is risky. Here several independent planners each propose how the vehicle should move based on the same sensor information, and an arbiter weighs their proposals before issuing the final steering and speed commands, improving safety and robustness.

US10793024.headline: Car seats that adjust to the occupant's build
US10793024.summary: A seat that suits one person may be uncomfortable for another of different size. The seat builds a digital model of the occupant's body, analyses how they sit, and automatically adjusts properties such as firmness or shape through built-in motors to fit them better.

WO2019089578.headline: Identifying typefaces from a photograph
WO2019089578.summary: Designers often see a font they like in a photo or advert but cannot name it. A machine-learning system trained on many fonts, including text placed over real-world backgrounds, recognises which typeface appears in an image.

US10809704.headline: Predicting factory alarms from performance data
US10809704.summary: Industrial plants generate streams of alarms and performance indicators that operators struggle to connect. The system mines historical records to learn which patterns of alarms and indicators go together, then matches live data against them to warn operators of a developing problem or predict an imminent alarm.

EP3704056.headline: Simpler tap for dispensing drinks from containers
EP3704056.summary: A countertop dispenser holds a drinks container upside down in a cradle and connects it, via an adaptor, to a self-venting tap. This lets drinks be poured smoothly without the container collapsing or needing a separate air vent.

CN109728224.headline: Adjustable battery trolley for rail vehicles
CN109728224.summary: Batteries for trains are moved in a wheeled container that must fit guide slots of varying width on different vehicles. The two wheel assemblies slide along a guide beam so their spacing can be adjusted, letting one trolley serve many types of rail vehicle.

EP3675008.headline: Finding office tasks worth automating with software robots
EP3675008.summary: Companies want to automate repetitive computer work but struggle to identify which tasks qualify. The method records how employees interact with their computers, splits the recordings into individual tasks, groups similar ones, ranks them as automation candidates and can then build the software robots to perform them.

EP3567967.headline: Clearer rules for phones sending data on 5G
EP3567967.summary: In 5G networks a phone may be assigned a frequency band without the control channel needed to signal beam direction. The method defines how the phone should behave in that situation, avoiding ambiguous instructions from the network and keeping uplink transmissions reliable.

WO2019090268.headline: Training workers using video that recognises actions
WO2019090268.summary: Cameras and sensors on a factory floor, in a hospital or warehouse can watch how tasks are performed. Machine learning recognises the individual actions and sequences, and this understanding is used to give workers context-specific training and feedback.

EP3777084.headline: Securing how apps access mobile network services
EP3777084.summary: Mobile operators increasingly let third-party applications use network functions through standard software interfaces. The proposal sets out security procedures covering the whole lifecycle, from registering an application and publishing a service to authorising, authenticating and withdrawing access, to prevent misuse.

EP4119605.headline: Plant-based plastic for shoe soles and foams
EP4119605.summary: EVA is a flexible plastic widely used in trainers, foams and packaging, normally made from fossil fuels. This version uses ethylene derived at least partly from renewable plant sources, offering a measurable bio-based content while keeping the hardness needed for everyday products.

EP3790884.headline: New chemical compounds for treating cancer
EP3790884.summary: A family of ring-shaped chemical compounds is proposed for treating disorders in which cells multiply uncontrollably, such as cancer, together with methods for making them and formulating them as medicines.

CN109802089.headline: Better filling and conditioning of giant batteries
CN109802089.summary: Very large single battery cells are hard to fill evenly with electrolyte, which shortens their life. A step-by-step procedure of filling, resting, partial charging and repeated vacuum treatment ensures the liquid soaks in uniformly, improving consistency and extending the number of charge cycles.

WO2019103837.headline: Linking wind-turbine generators through a shared power line
WO2019103837.summary: Several generators of the type used in wind turbines are connected together via a common direct-current line, with a back-up power source and energy storage attached to it. This arrangement helps the system keep running smoothly and share power between units.

US11593585.headline: Automatically finding and cropping objects in photos
US11593585.summary: Software that scans documents or products from photos must first locate the object against its background. By sampling colours from the background and foreground, labelling each pixel, and tracing the resulting outline, the method finds the object's edges and crops the image automatically.

EP3807269.headline: New brain-targeting compounds for medicines
EP3807269.summary: A family of chemical compounds that act on a particular receptor in the brain (GABA-A alpha5) is described, along with formulations and uses as medicines. The abstract gives little further detail.

EP3732932.headline: Steering mobile phone masts mounted on drones
EP3732932.summary: Mobile coverage can be extended using base stations carried on drones or vehicles. A central controller gathers information about radio conditions and plans approximate flight paths both for the moving cells that serve users and for those that relay their traffic back to the network.

DE102018204346.headline: Insulated screws for safer battery connections
DE102018204346.summary: Connecting battery cells with metal straps and screws leaves live metal exposed. Here the screw head carries an insulating sleeve that extends beyond it, reducing the risk of short circuits or electric shock during assembly and maintenance of vehicle batteries.

EP3802544.headline: New chemical compounds for possible medicines
EP3802544.summary: A group of novel chemical compounds and their pharmaceutical formulations are described for therapeutic use. The abstract does not specify the diseases targeted.

DE102018201438.headline: Flexible fabric strap connects battery cells
DE102018201438.summary: Rigid metal connectors between battery cells can crack under vibration or as cells expand. This connector uses a conductive fabric band with metal sleeves at the ends for the fastening screws, giving a flexible yet reliable electrical link.

CN110048050.headline: Lighter, sturdier housing for car battery packs
CN110048050.summary: An electric-vehicle battery pack housing has an upper shell joined to a lower shell whose floor is reinforced by side and cross beams forming a rectangular frame. The design aims to be robust while keeping weight down.

CN110071240.headline: Guides that help slot battery boxes into racks
CN110071240.summary: In large energy-storage installations, battery boxes slide into racks and can jam or be damaged if misaligned. Matching male and female guide pieces on the box and rack steer the box into its correct position even if pushed in slightly askew, and hold it steady during transport.

WO2019191695.headline: Drag-and-drop design tool for energy plants
WO2019191695.summary: Planning a central energy plant for a campus or district is complex. A visual tool lets users drag symbols for energy sources, sub-plants, storage and loads onto a workspace, blocks invalid connections, and then simulates the plant's operation to support design and budgeting decisions.

EP4403174.headline: New chemical compounds for treating disease
EP4403174.summary: A family of chemical compounds, their salts and formulations are described for use in treating disease. The abstract does not specify which conditions.

US10380236.headline: AI that labels parts of free-form text
US10380236.summary: Much useful information sits in unstructured text such as notes or messages. A neural network reads the text and attaches labels to fragments, for example identifying names, dates or product details, and is designed to capture relationships between labels that lie far apart in the text.

EP3749538.headline: Balanced hybrid scooter with electric assist
EP3749538.summary: Adding an electric motor and battery to a small petrol-powered scooter or motorcycle can upset its balance and ground clearance. Placing the motor and its power source within the area between the rider's and passenger's footrests keeps weight well distributed and ground clearance suitable for city riding.

WO2019155713.headline: Stopping fires spreading between battery cells
WO2019155713.summary: When one cell in an electric-vehicle battery overheats, heat can spread to its neighbours and cause a chain reaction. Separators between cells combine a rigid frame, which keeps the spacing fixed, with a soft insulating core that absorbs cell swelling while blocking heat transfer.

DE102018208133.headline: Simpler terminals for joining car battery cells
DE102018208133.summary: Each battery cell has a flat terminal on its lid with a tab projecting beyond the edge. Tabs of neighbouring cells can be joined end to end, connecting the cells electrically while keeping them physically apart, simplifying assembly of high-voltage vehicle batteries.

EP3830949.headline: Hidden connectors for solar roof tiles
EP3830949.summary: Solar roof tiles must link electrically to one another without spoiling the roof's appearance. A metal plug set into a hole in the tile's rear glass connects the internal wiring to the outside, allowing neighbouring tiles to be wired together from behind.

DE102018203578.headline: Insulated connectors reduce battery short circuits
DE102018203578.summary: Metal straps joining battery cells are coated with an insulating layer that also forms a cup around each fastening screw head. This shields live parts, reducing the risk of short circuits during assembly and operation of vehicle batteries.

CN110212125.headline: Side outlets save space in battery modules
CN110212125.summary: Battery modules usually have their output terminals on top, which can waste space in a tight installation. A wiring board with a busbar that bends down the module's side moves the terminals to the side, allowing more flexible, compact arrangements.

EP3999042.headline: Modified CBD molecules for new medicines
EP3999042.summary: Cannabidiol (CBD), a non-intoxicating component of cannabis, is used to treat various conditions but with limited effectiveness. Chemically modified versions of CBD, and methods of making them, aim to deliver stronger therapeutic effects.

EP3626522.headline: Lighter backrest frame for vehicle seats
EP3626522.summary: A vehicle seat backrest built around a central spine with side stability elements channels the loads from a seated person down into the seat base. The structure is intended for seats in lorries and other commercial vehicles.

EP3626523.headline: Pivoting backrest for lorry cab seats
EP3626523.summary: A commercial-vehicle seat has a backrest built around a central spine that pivots about an axis set above the seat cushion. This lets the backrest tilt in a way suited to the demands of lorry and machinery cabs.

US11084404.headline: Car seats with built-in heating and ventilation
US11084404.summary: Comfort in a car depends on seat temperature. The seat contains layered padding through which a pump drives air, with a heating element near the surface, so the seat can be both warmed and ventilated from within.

WO2019183153.headline: Teaching inspection AI with hand-edited defect images
WO2019183153.summary: Automated inspection systems for chips or other products need many examples of defects to learn from, but real examples are scarce. Users edit real images to add realistic defects via a graphical interface, and these synthetic images are added to the training data for the machine-learning model.

US10437712.headline: Automatically writing tests for software interfaces
US10437712.summary: Software services expose interfaces that other programs call, and testing them by hand is laborious. By reading a formal description of the interface, the tool identifies each function and its parameters and automatically generates a set of tests to check it works.

WO2019200317.headline: Security software that learns normal behaviour
WO2019200317.summary: A security platform builds models of how users, devices and other entities normally behave, keeps updating them as conditions change, and raises alerts when patterns of events depart from the norm.

EP3782090.headline: Smarter autocomplete for chat assistants
EP3782090.summary: Typing requests to a digital assistant is slow. As the user types a partial request, a personalised language model guesses the likely intent and details, offers completions, and when the user picks one the assistant carries out the task straight away.

EP3864573.headline: Expanding driving-camera data to train AI
EP3864573.summary: Self-driving systems need vast numbers of labelled images. Images from vehicle cameras are altered in ways that preserve the camera's optical characteristics, and these modified copies inherit the original labels, cheaply enlarging the training set for the predictive model.

US10750452.headline: Sensor chips that sip power while waiting
US10750452.summary: Wearables and other gadgets waste battery keeping their processor awake to watch sensors. A low-power hub polls the sensors on a slow clock while the main processor sleeps, waking it only when a sensor registers activity.

EP3706275.headline: Modelling the wider grid a utility cannot see
EP3706275.summary: Grid operators have detailed measurements of their own network but not of neighbouring networks. The method builds a simplified stand-in for the external network from measurements at the boundary, then tunes its parameters until the overall model matches reality closely enough for reliable monitoring.

EP3811682.headline: Keeping emergency calls working across network types
EP3811682.summary: A phone may be connected to a mobile network both via a cellular link and via Wi-Fi, and registered for emergency services on one of them. The method specifies how the phone should behave in this situation so emergency service remains available.

EP3613138.headline: Roof tiles that generate solar power
EP3613138.summary: Conventional solar panels sit on top of a roof. Here the photovoltaic cells are sealed between a glass front and a protective back cover so that each unit acts as a roof tile in its own right, keeping out the weather while producing electricity.

EP3897780.headline: Simpler self-injecting device for medicines
EP3897780.summary: A hand-held device delivers a drug through a needle. Turning a drive wheel first unlocks a plunger rod, which then advances to deploy the needle and push out the medicine, giving a controlled sequence of actions for patients injecting themselves.

US10579370.headline: Breaking big software into smaller services
US10579370.summary: Large monolithic applications are hard to maintain and update. The tool scans the application's code, finds small self-contained pieces of functionality, groups related ones and recommends how to split them into independent microservices, which the user can then choose to generate.

EP3633511.headline: Finding the root cause of IT outages automatically
EP3633511.summary: When a business application slows down or fails, pinpointing the cause among thousands of servers and services is slow. The system maintains a map of how components connect and, when a problem is detected, searches only related components for recent anomalies to explain it.

EP3690762.headline: Visual check on how a risk-scoring AI behaves
EP3690762.summary: Machine-learning models used for risk assessment, such as fraud or credit decisions, can be opaque. The system analyses the model's features against defined constraints and training data, and displays visual indicators that summarise how well the model performs.

EP4097110.headline: New compounds to calm harmful inflammation
EP4097110.summary: An enzyme called RIP2 kinase drives inflammatory responses in several diseases. Ring-shaped molecules that block this enzyme are proposed for diagnosing, preventing or treating these conditions.

WO2020036209.headline: Smoother powered sliding for vehicle seats
WO2020036209.summary: Powered car seats slide on rails driven by a threaded screw, and slack in the mechanism can cause rattling. A built-in element absorbs this play between the seat frame and the screw, with a lock to hold the seat in position.

EP3844247.headline: Turning waste plastic into liquid fuel
EP3844247.summary: Plastic waste is heated without oxygen at several hundred degrees to break it down into vapour, which is cooled in four stages to well below freezing. The resulting liquid is collected as fuel while the remaining gases are separated, in a process claimed to be simple, economical and energy efficient.

EP3850596.headline: Space-saving vending machine on stilts
EP3850596.summary: Vending machines take up valuable floor space. This design raises the product compartment on a support structure, leaving the space beneath free for other uses or for people to walk through, with an automated system delivering products down to the dispensing port.

EP3887912.headline: Cloud-updated monitoring of factory equipment
EP3887912.summary: Industrial plants monitor machinery for signs of wear or failure using digital models of each asset. Here those models live in the cloud, and engineers can submit new monitoring schemes which are turned into updated models and used to recommend control actions.

EP4107235.headline: Making acetylene from natural gas with recycled lime
EP4107235.summary: Acetylene, a chemical building block, is produced by heating methane to split it into carbon and hydrogen, reacting the carbon with lime to form calcium carbide, and adding water to release acetylene. The lime is recovered and reused, closing the loop.

EP3858007.headline: Letting idle phones sleep longer between checks
EP3858007.summary: Phones periodically wake to check whether the network is trying to reach them, draining battery. By grouping devices with similar characteristics and sending a short group wake-up signal only when a message is waiting, devices can rest longer and save power.

WO2020069590.headline: Ceramic tiles made with chemical-industry sludge
WO2020069590.summary: Brine sludge is a solid waste from chemical production that is costly to dispose of. Mixing a few per cent of it into ceramic raw materials, then pressing and firing the mass, produces coatings and panels for construction, turning a waste stream into building material.

EP3734453.headline: Mix-and-match chips for edge computing
EP3734453.summary: Edge computing devices near users must handle widely varying workloads. By building hardware from small separable chip components (chiplets) for processing, memory, storage and acceleration, the device can assemble the configuration each incoming workload needs.

EP4234555.headline: Efficient route to making a blood-clot drug
EP4234555.summary: Highly efficient methods are provided for preparing key intermediate chemicals in the synthesis of a complex pharmaceutical compound. The approach is said to be broadly applicable to related compounds with different substituents.

WO2021236072.headline: Fridge ice bin that stays put yet removable
WO2021236072.summary: In a refrigerator ice dispenser, the rotating screw that pushes ice out can also push the removable ice bin loose. A latch applies a counter-force so the bin stays in place during dispensing, while the user can still remove it with a firmer pull.

US10719301.headline: Teamwork tools for building image and video AI
US10719301.summary: Developing machine-learning models for photos and video involves many rounds of experiments. This environment lets teams annotate and manage training media, configure and run training and test experiments, and inspect performance and sample results to decide how to improve the next iteration.

EP3911596.headline: Linking two chemical processes to make methanol
EP3911596.summary: Methanol is made from syngas, a mixture of hydrogen and carbon monoxide. By combining a partial-oxidation reactor with a hydrocarbon cracking unit that produces olefins, the hydrogen-rich by-product from cracking is used to enrich the syngas, improving its composition for methanol production.

WO2021118644.headline: Faster device-to-device Wi-Fi without channel hopping
WO2021118644.summary: Devices linked directly over Wi-Fi normally share the same channel as their router, forcing them to switch back and forth. Here the router link stays on the 2.4 GHz band while the direct link moves to a separate 5 GHz channel, running in parallel to reduce delays and increase throughput.

JP2020141980.headline: Auto-rapid-fire button for arcade game effects
JP2020141980.summary: In Japanese pachinko-style game machines, players are prompted to press a button repeatedly to trigger on-screen effects. The machine recognises a long press as equivalent to rapid tapping and plays the corresponding effect, making the button feature more convenient.

WO2020181892.headline: Compact loudspeaker with two diaphragms
WO2020181892.summary: A small speaker for phones and other devices places vibrating diaphragms on both sides of a single magnet assembly, each driven by its own coil. A connecting piece keeps the coil moving straight, allowing more sound from a compact unit.

US10791063.headline: Analysing sensor data without moving it off-site
US10791063.summary: Internet-connected sensors generate data that is often too sensitive or voluminous to send to a central cloud. The system discovers data sources at the network edge, collects descriptive metadata, and coordinates analysis across distributed nodes so that raw data stays within its local zone.

EP3947081.headline: Standardising sensor data for self-driving cars
EP3947081.summary: Self-driving cars combine readings from many different sensors. Before the car interprets its surroundings, the raw data is normalised, geometrically corrected and filtered into a common form, making the subsequent perception step more consistent and reliable.

US10810508.headline: Learning machine operating states from sensor histories
US10810508.summary: Industrial equipment emits many on/off signals and numeric readings, but which combinations represent distinct operating states is often unclear. The method groups periods with the same on/off pattern into states and trains a model on the numeric readings, so past and future states can be classified automatically.

EP3809592.headline: Pinpointing faults across solar panel arrays
EP3809592.summary: Faults in large solar installations are hard to locate and existing checks detect only one type at a time. A neural network trained on simulated data covering many fault scenarios learns to detect different fault types and identify where in the array they occur.

EP4097210.headline: Laundry liquid that stays colourful in clear bottles
EP4097210.summary: Liquid detergents sold in transparent bottles can discolour. A formulation combining cleaning agents, a small amount of a specific blue-violet dye and an additive that binds iron strongly keeps the product's appearance stable.

US10838783.headline: Keeping management dashboards in sync with storage systems
US10838783.summary: Data-storage management software shows a simplified view of many underlying components. By mapping dependencies between the displayed objects and backend components, the system can update exactly the right displayed items whenever a backend notification arrives.

US10956181.headline: Computers that follow how-to videos automatically
US10956181.summary: Instructional videos show how to perform tasks on a computer, but viewers must still carry out each step by hand. The software transcribes the narration, reads on-screen text, spots simulated clicks and keystrokes, builds a timeline and converts each step into commands the computer executes itself.

EP3972589.headline: New drugs for heart, kidney and diabetes conditions
EP3972589.summary: Compounds that activate a receptor involved in regulating blood pressure and fluid balance are proposed as treatments for high blood pressure, heart failure, kidney disease and diabetes.

US11025732.headline: Keeping cloud log-ins alive automatically
US11025732.summary: Tools that manage devices through cloud providers rely on session tokens that expire. A session manager tracks each token's lifespan and uses stored credentials to refresh it before expiry, so actions on devices can be carried out without interruptions or repeated log-ins.

EP3983943.headline: Image recognition that runs inside the browser
EP3983943.summary: Classifying images usually means sending them to a remote server. Here several machine-learning models sharing a common base are downloaded once to the user's device and run in the web browser, so later images are classified locally without further requests.

EP3990091.headline: Improved manufacture of a drug ingredient
EP3990091.summary: A method for preparing a specific pharmaceutical compound in its hydrochloride salt form, along with the intermediate chemicals used along the way, is described. The abstract does not state the drug's intended use.

EP3842124.headline: Air purifier that strips carbon dioxide from rooms
EP3842124.summary: Indoor air can accumulate carbon dioxide. This device draws air through a unit where acid and base solutions capture the gas and vent it outside, regenerates the chemicals by electrodialysis, and also condenses humidity and splits the water by electrolysis.

WO2021134035.headline: Making hydrogen from fuels without external heat
WO2021134035.summary: Hydrogen is usually produced by steam reforming, which needs large energy input. Here liquid fuels such as naphtha or diesel pass first through a combustion zone with a special catalyst, whose heat then drives steam reforming in a second zone, yielding hydrogen-rich gas in a self-sustaining process.

US11921815.headline: Fitting customer data to ready-made AI templates
US11921815.summary: Businesses wanting machine-learning solutions often have data that does not match what pre-built models expect. The system picks a model template for the stated problem, maps the customer's data to a schema, detects mismatches and works out what extra information is needed to realign them.

US10957229.headline: Smarter use of curved phone screen edges
US10957229.summary: Phones with displays that curve round the edges need to decide what to show there. The device judges whether content suits the edges and whether they are covered by the user's hand, extending suitable content onto the edges only when they are unobstructed.

US10963887.headline: Letting shops contact customers without their real details
US10963887.summary: Customers paying by card may not want every merchant to have their phone number or email. A payment service that already holds a customer's contact details generates a stand-in contact address for each new merchant, who can message the customer through it without seeing the real information.

EP4111290.headline: Cache memory that switches off unused parts
EP4111290.summary: Processor caches store address tags whose size depends on how much memory the system has. By making some tag storage columns switchable, columns not needed for a given system can be powered off, saving energy.

EP4018350.headline: Spotting wasted power from signal glitches in chips
EP4018350.summary: Brief unintended signal flickers, or glitches, waste power in digital chips. By shifting recorded signal waveforms according to calculated timing delays, the tool identifies where glitches occur in a chip design before it is manufactured.

EP4046057.headline: Helping digital assistants parse what users mean
EP4046057.summary: Digital assistants must turn spoken requests into actions. A structured vocabulary breaks each request into actions, objects and attributes nested within one another, which is passed to the service that performs the task and shapes how results are presented back to the user.

EP3901237.headline: Squeezing more plastics feedstock from heavy oil residues
EP3901237.summary: Heavy residues from oil refining are cracked under severe conditions to yield more light olefins, the building blocks of plastics. A by-product stream of four-carbon molecules is further processed into aromatics, raising the overall yield of petrochemical feedstocks.

EP4133545.headline: Shock-proof packaging for battery cells
EP4133545.summary: Battery modules in vehicles suffer vibration and impacts. Cells sit in holders pressed by a flexible member, with a support structure and thermal interface transferring heat to the casing, making the module mechanically stable and vibration resistant.

EP3920034.headline: Networked memory devices that stay in sync
EP3920034.summary: Data centres increasingly pool memory across machines. A storage device with two controllers, one speaking a cache-coherent protocol over the network and another handling a local memory, keeps data consistent while scaling capacity.

EP4204361.headline: New porous mineral for chemical processing
EP4204361.summary: Zeolites are porous crystalline materials used as catalysts and filters. A new aluminium-rich variant, SSZ-123, is made using a specially designed organic molecule as a template and can be used for converting organic compounds or separating substances.

US11017139.headline: Checking two chip designs behave identically
US11017139.summary: Chip designers must confirm that a modified circuit behaves exactly like the original. The tool picks values for internal control signals, generates inputs that bring the circuits into those states, simulates both and compares them, while also ruling out states that can never arise.

EP4078488.headline: AI review of automated software test workflows
EP4078488.summary: Software robots are increasingly used to run automated tests, but their test workflows can be poorly designed. An AI model checks each workflow against predefined rules, calculates quality metrics and suggests corrections.

EP4081496.headline: Catalyst that turns light hydrocarbons into olefins
EP4081496.summary: Light olefins, used to make plastics, can be produced by cracking small hydrocarbon molecules. A catalyst combining zeolites with pores of several different sizes and a small amount of a metal additive aims to improve this conversion.

US11061457.headline: Sharing charger power across USB-C ports
US11061457.summary: Multi-port chargers must divide limited power among whatever devices are plugged in. A master controller detects which ports are in use and each device's needs, then allocates power dynamically, regardless of the order in which devices were connected.

EP4168715.headline: Sanitising rooms automatically when they are empty
EP4168715.summary: Shared spaces in offices, hospitals and schools can spread pathogens. Occupancy sensors tell a controller when a room is empty, and it then triggers a sanitising device to disinfect surfaces at a suitable time, reducing exposure risk without disturbing occupants.

US11100034.headline: Safer power switching for USB-C chargers
US11100034.summary: USB-C cables can carry high power, so a short circuit or current flowing the wrong way can damage a phone or charger. This circuit controls two power switches in series and shuts them off quickly when it detects a fault, using cheaper low-voltage components. It is aimed at USB-C power delivery controllers.

US11550374.headline: Cooling electronics using the weather forecast
US11550374.summary: Computer equipment can overheat when the surrounding air warms up. This system pulls in local weather data and, together with a model of the device and a lookup table, works out the temperature at which cooling should kick in. If the device runs hotter than that threshold, it switches on a connected cooling unit.

EP3971267.headline: Making cleaner industrial solvents from petroleum
EP3971267.summary: Many paints, inks and cleaning products need solvents that are low in aromatic compounds, which are a health and odour concern. This refinery process treats several petroleum streams with hydrogen and catalysts, then strips, filters and distils them to produce multiple grades of very low-aromatic solvent, converting unwanted aromatics into more benign molecules.

WO2022187919.headline: Adding fuel briquettes to iron ore pellets
WO2022187919.summary: Iron ore is formed into pellets that must be baked hard in a kiln before use in steelmaking. This method mixes fuel briquettes into the bed of unfired pellets before they enter the kiln, so the fuel burns among the pellets during firing. It is a simpler way of supplying heat to the process.

WO2021195728.headline: Longer-lasting catalyst for making hydrogen
WO2021195728.summary: Hydrogen is mostly produced by reacting natural gas with steam over a catalyst, which gradually clogs with carbon deposits. This catalyst combines nickel, molybdenum and tungsten, optionally on an alumina support, and is far more resistant to that clogging. It could cut downtime and costs in hydrogen and synthesis gas production.

EP4132580.headline: Stable formulation of a cancer antibody drug
EP4132580.summary: Antibody medicines must be mixed into a liquid that keeps them potent during storage. This covers formulations of anti-CD47 antibodies, a class being developed for cancer treatment, at usable concentrations with a stable shelf life.

US12099940.headline: Spotting unusual behaviour in payment data
US12099940.summary: Banks and card networks need to detect fraud among huge volumes of transactions. This approach borrows techniques from language modelling to turn streams of events, such as card payments, into compact numerical representations of a person's typical behaviour. Current activity can then be compared against the historical pattern to flag anything out of character.

EP4143732.headline: All-in-one platform for team workflows
EP4143732.summary: Organisations juggle documents, chat, email, scheduling, cost tracking and customer records in separate tools. This software brings those functions together in a table-based workspace that can identify data types automatically, send notifications, manage permissions and turn data into charts and dashboards for collaborative work.

EP4157274.headline: Safely combining a cortisol drug with diabetes pills
EP4157274.summary: Relacorilant, used for excess cortisol and some cancers, was expected in laboratory tests to interfere with how the body clears common drugs such as the diabetes medicines tolbutamide, glimepiride and glipizide. Human studies found no such effect, so the drugs can be taken together at normal doses without dose reductions.

EP4243825.headline: Heart failure treatment for specific patient groups
