EP4243825.summary: Heart failure weakens the heart's pumping ability. This covers treating heart failure with the drug omecamtiv mecarbil in patients who show particular additional clinical features, using a therapeutically effective dose of the compound or its salts and hydrates.

US11937230.headline: Boosting Wi-Fi range under power limits
US11937230.summary: Regulators cap how much wireless power can be transmitted per unit of frequency, which limits range. This method spreads a small chunk of data across scattered frequency slices within a wider band, rather than one contiguous block, so a device can send at higher total power while still obeying the limit.

EP4175430.headline: Easier-to-swap cooling fans for network gear
EP4175430.summary: Rack-mounted network switches rely on fans that occasionally need replacing while the equipment keeps running. This fan module has an inner cassette holding the fans and controller that latches into an outer frame fixed to the chassis, so technicians can swap the fans without removing the whole unit.

EP4023473.headline: Hydrogen fuel cell motorbike layout
EP4023473.summary: Fitting a hydrogen fuel cell and gas canister onto a two-wheeler is a packaging challenge. This frame design mounts the fuel canister low in the centre of the bike and the fuel cell stack at the top of the rear frame, lowering and balancing the centre of gravity while making refuelling, assembly and servicing easier.

PH12021050316.headline: Quieter, longer-lasting oil for electric car axles
PH12021050316.summary: Electric vehicles use compact e-axles whose gears and motors need special lubrication and run quietly enough that gear noise becomes noticeable. This transmission lubricant combines a base oil of suitable viscosity with a particular additive mix to suppress noise and improve durability in e-axle applications.

US12184730.headline: Showing how costly each fraud rule is
US12184730.summary: Payment companies run thousands of automated rules to approve or block transactions in real time, and some rule variables are far slower to compute than others. This tool assigns each variable a processing weight, suggests similar cheaper alternatives, and shows the weights to rule authors so they can write faster, less costly rules.

EP4202020.headline: Turning waste fats into jet fuel
EP4202020.summary: Vegetable oils, animal fats and used cooking oil can be converted into renewable fuels. This two-step process, hydrotreating followed by hydrocracking, uses partially reduced catalysts without added sulphur to produce bio-jet fuel suitable for blending with conventional kerosene, along with renewable naphtha, diesel and heavy paraffins.

WO2022051180.headline: Smoother power sharing in multi-port USB-C chargers
WO2022051180.summary: Chargers with several USB-C ports switch power on and off thousands of times a second, and if all ports switch in step they create electrical noise and stress. This controller staggers the timing of each port's switching clock so the ports take turns, reducing interference and smoothing demand on the power supply.

EP4217095.headline: Air purifier that also removes carbon dioxide
EP4217095.summary: Indoor air purifiers typically remove dust and odours but not carbon dioxide, which builds up in closed rooms. This purifier adds a unit through which incoming air passes alongside an alkaline solution that chemically captures carbon dioxide before the cleaned air is released back into the room.

EP4232444.headline: New drugs targeting a common cancer mutation
EP4232444.summary: A mutation known as KRAS G12C drives many lung, pancreatic and bowel cancers and was long considered impossible to target with drugs. These spiro-shaped compounds block the mutant protein and are proposed as treatments for such cancers.

EP4323369.headline: New compounds for treating lupus
EP4323369.summary: Lupus is an autoimmune disease in which the immune system attacks the body's own tissues, affecting the skin and internal organs. This covers a family of thienopyrrole compounds, and medicines containing them, intended to treat or prevent autoimmune and inflammatory conditions including systemic and skin lupus.

EP4337196.headline: More stable crystal form of a cancer drug
EP4337196.summary: Drugs that block the BTK enzyme are used for blood cancers and immune disorders, but a drug's crystal form affects how well it stores and is absorbed. This covers co-crystal forms of a BTK inhibitor, how they are characterised and how they are made.

EP4112702.headline: Taming corrosive crude oil before coking
EP4112702.summary: Some heavy crude oils contain high levels of naphthenic acids that corrode refinery equipment. This three-stage pre-treatment heats the oil to break down acids, reacts the remainder with methanol, then filters through spent catalyst, so the cleaned residue can be processed in a delayed coker into lighter fuels.

EP4347575.headline: Drugs that block bile acid recycling
EP4347575.summary: Bile acids made by the liver are recycled from the gut, and blocking that recycling can help with liver, digestive and metabolic diseases. These benzothiazepine compounds inhibit the transporters that recycle bile acids and are proposed for treating cardiovascular, liver, gastrointestinal and glucose and fat metabolism disorders.

EP4306619.headline: Right-sizing chemicals when recycling liquefied plastic
EP4306619.summary: Waste plastic melted into oil contains acids and impurities that must be neutralised before it can be refined into new products. This method measures the acidity of each batch and uses it, together with the water-to-oil ratio, to calculate exactly how much alkaline solution to add during heat treatment to hit a target pH.

WO2023276755.headline: Turning plant waste into solid fuel
WO2023276755.summary: Woody and agricultural biomass is bulky and hard to burn efficiently. This system uses the water already inside the plant material to explode its fibres apart under pressure in a continuous process, then dries the result and presses it into a solid fuel suitable for power stations or boilers.

KR20220112710.headline: Several phones casting to one big screen
KR20220112710.summary: Normally only one device at a time can wirelessly cast its screen to a display. This system lets several phones, tablets or laptops each send part of their content to a large screen, where a controller synchronises the pieces, along with any locally generated content, into a single combined video picture.

US11574050.headline: Shielding backup storage from ransomware
US11574050.summary: Ransomware increasingly targets backup systems so victims cannot recover their files. This method installs a filter at start-up on the backup server that watches every request made to the software controlling the backup storage, lets through only authorised requests and silently ignores the rest, so attackers cannot encrypt or delete backups.

EP4392180.headline: Better catalyst for making plastics feedstock
EP4392180.summary: Olefins such as ethylene, the building blocks of plastics, are made by stripping hydrogen from simple hydrocarbons. This catalyst, a mixed oxide of molybdenum, vanadium, niobium and bismuth with a specific crystal structure, is designed to carry out that conversion using oxygen at lower energy cost.

EP4396651.headline: Smart glasses that share what you see
EP4396651.summary: Smart glasses make it awkward to compose messages. With this feature, when a wearer looks at a marked real-world object for long enough, the glasses capture a 3D snapshot of it; every time the object reappears in view, a representation of it is sent to a friend's display as if the object itself had been shared.

EP4395779.headline: Oral drug for multiple sclerosis
EP4395779.summary: Multiple sclerosis is a disease in which the immune system damages nerves in the brain and spinal cord. This covers the use of the compound LOU064, or its salts, as a treatment for the condition.

JP7616927.headline: Systems for amusement park rides
JP7616927.summary: Covers systems for use in amusement parks; the published summary gives no further detail of the problem addressed or the approach taken.

EP4376800.headline: Aluminium-free antiperspirant
EP4376800.summary: Most antiperspirants rely on aluminium salts to block sweat, which some consumers wish to avoid. These personal care formulations reduce sweating without added aluminium actives, instead combining humectants, thickeners and alpha hydroxy acids in a carrier base.

EP4270553.headline: Nozzles to push fuel evenly through fuel cells
EP4270553.summary: In a stack of solid oxide fuel cells, fuel gas slows down as it travels through the stack, starving the far end. This feed assembly adds narrowing nozzles along the supply path so the gas accelerates as it enters each stack, giving it enough momentum to overcome the resistance and distribute evenly.

US12026521.headline: USB signal booster that works in both directions
US12026521.summary: Long USB cables weaken high-speed signals, so repeaters are used to refresh them, but a repeater normally needs to know which end is the host. This repeater watches how long activity persists on a port and, once a threshold is passed, automatically reconfigures its internal resistors so it works whichever way the devices are connected.

EP4419633.headline: Blending two biofuels for better diesel
EP4419633.summary: Diesel made from woody biomass by hydropyrolysis ignites too slowly on its own, falling short of fuel standards. Blending it with a second renewable diesel made from fats and oils lifts the ignition quality of the mixture above the required threshold, producing a usable fully renewable diesel.

US11617951.headline: Automatic highlight summaries of video game sessions
US11617951.summary: After a gaming session players want to review what happened without rewatching everything. This system logs in-game events with timestamps and links them to captured clips, then builds an interactive summary with a timeline, an annotated map, statistics and trends, including for whole teams, so players can jump straight to key moments.

EP4427203.headline: Finding visually matching shots for film editing
EP4427203.summary: A match cut is an editing technique that joins two shots with similar composition or motion, and finding candidates by hand is slow. This software splits videos into shots, removes duplicates, encodes each shot numerically and compares the encodings, using fast approximate search to suggest pairs of shots that would cut together well.

US11944955.headline: Tougher catalyst for turning acidic oils into biofuel
US11944955.summary: Used cooking oils and other cheap biofuel feedstocks are acidic and quickly wear out the catalysts that process them. This catalyst, based on sulphated zirconia with cerium, is more active and resists that deactivation, making it better suited to pre-treating acidic feedstocks for biofuel production.

US11570073.headline: Telling customers when network services fail
US11570073.summary: Businesses buy multiple network services from a provider but often have no quick way to know which one has failed. The provider's edge router inspects passing traffic to work out the health of each service, then embeds the status in a standard neighbour-discovery message sent to the customer's own router.

EP4469196.headline: Feeding waste plastic into oil refineries
EP4469196.summary: Recycling mixed waste plastic chemically is difficult because molten plastic is thick and hard to handle. This system melts the plastic in one extruder, dissolves it in oil in a second mixing extruder and feeds the resulting solution into an existing refinery oil stream, so standard refinery units can convert it into new fuels and chemicals.

EP4387609.headline: New compounds for inflammatory disease
EP4387609.summary: A protein called CCR6 helps steer immune cells and is implicated in inflammatory conditions such as psoriasis. This covers aryl sulfonyl piperidine compounds that block CCR6 and are proposed for treating diseases driven by it.

WO2023028964.headline: Faster video compression on graphics chips
WO2023028964.summary: Compressing video requires choosing, for every patch of each frame, the best prediction method and block size, which is normally done one step at a time. This technique works out shared intermediate pixel values and then evaluates the options for different block sizes simultaneously, speeding up encoding for streaming and game capture.

US12031769.headline: Simpler way to fix bins to fridge doors
US12031769.summary: Shelves and bins on the inside of a refrigerator door need secure, adjustable mounting. This design moulds channels into the door's inner liner and fits a strip with a row of holes inside each channel, so bins can be hooked into the holes at a choice of heights.

EP4409378.headline: Keeping idle processors warm to prevent damage
EP4409378.summary: Chips that repeatedly swing between hot and cold while idling and working suffer stress at their soldered joints and packaging. This processor monitors its own temperature and, when idle, deliberately switches off power-saving features and tweaks its settings to hold the temperature within a steady, slightly elevated band, reducing wear.

EP4430533.headline: AI that tunes chipmaking recipes per wafer
EP4430533.summary: Semiconductor wafers vary slightly in their properties, yet process tools usually follow a fixed recipe. Here each recipe carries an identifier code linking it to the wafer's characteristics; a machine-learning module looks up the matching data and adjusts the recipe accordingly before the wafer is processed.

US12020128.headline: Training AI on shared data without exposing it
US12020128.summary: Companies want to combine data for machine learning without handing over their raw records. This method shares a provider's training data and functions into a customer's database account as a read-only instance; the customer trains a model there and scores its own private data, so neither party sees the other's underlying information.

US12012560.headline: Making renewable jet fuel from fats and oils
US12012560.summary: Aviation needs lower-carbon fuel that still meets strict standards. This process runs a feed made entirely from vegetable and animal fats and related compounds through a refinery's catalytic cracking unit, producing renewable kerosene rich in aromatics that meets jet fuel specifications when blended up to ten per cent without extra processing.

EP4554974.headline: Dosing schedules for a rare nerve disease
EP4554974.summary: Multifocal motor neuropathy is a rare condition causing progressive weakness as the immune system attacks motor nerves. This sets out methods and dosing regimens for treating it with an antibody that targets a specific part of a complement protein involved in that immune attack.

WO2024026203.headline: Faster ray tracing with compressible scene data
WO2024026203.summary: Realistic lighting in games uses ray tracing, which relies on a tree-like structure to find which objects a light ray hits. This technique builds alternative wider trees, estimates how well each would compress in memory, and picks the one that best balances speed and storage on the graphics chip.

EP4599311.headline: Smarter hibernation for laptops with worn batteries
EP4599311.summary: Laptops with ageing batteries can shut down abruptly, losing work. This approach records which tasks the user does not mind pausing, tracks battery health in each cell and current workload, and scores each task's penalty for being paused, then sends the least costly tasks to sleep or hibernation as the battery falls below set levels.

US12323530.headline: Splitting crypto wallet keys for security
US12323530.summary: Crypto wallets are vulnerable if a single private key is stolen. This system splits the key into parts, keeping one on the user's own device and another out of the wallet provider's reach, so blockchain transactions can be authorised securely without any one party holding the full key.

US12032935.headline: Checking cloud software lands in the right environment
US12032935.summary: Software often fails because it is deployed into a setting that lacks the resources or settings it assumes. This technique lets developers attach the required environmental conditions to a software component when it is written; the deployment system then automatically verifies the target environment meets those conditions before installing.

US11799480.headline: Switching between power supplies on a chip
US11799480.summary: Chips often run from several supply voltages and need to switch cleanly between them. This circuit uses a chain of transistors for each supply, all feeding one output; switching on one chain and off the others selects that supply, and the design scales easily to more supplies.

US12131152.headline: Scoring how portable software is
US12131152.summary: Moving an application to a different operating system is costly if the code depends heavily on the original one. This test runs the application, counts how many calls it makes to features unique to the host operating system, and turns that count into a portability score.

US11831315.headline: Cutting power waste in high-speed chip circuits
US11831315.summary: Fast signalling circuits inside chips are usually over-powered to guarantee they still work in worst-case manufacturing, voltage and temperature conditions. This design adds a temperature-compensating calibrator that adjusts the circuit to hit the target signal strength exactly, avoiding the wasted power of over-biasing.

US11954802.headline: Smoother 3D surfaces from voxel data
US11954802.summary: Converting a shape stored as a grid of 3D cells into a smooth polygon mesh often produces jagged results. This method places mesh vertices by estimating where the surface crosses each cell, then repeatedly nudges them to reduce the mismatch with the original data, giving a more accurate surface for 3D modelling and games.

US12050893.headline: Faster pause-and-resume code for processors
US12050893.summary: Programs that juggle many tasks use coroutines, routines that can pause and later resume, but implementing the pause is slow. This compiler recognises a special built-in suspend instruction in the source code and inserts efficient low-level machine code for it, improving performance of asynchronous software.

WO2024107609.headline: Automatic control for gravity-fed IV drips
WO2024107609.summary: Gravity-fed intravenous drips are normally adjusted by hand and can deliver fluid too fast or too slow. This device clips onto a standard IV line and combines a flow sensor, a flow controller and a user interface to actively monitor and regulate how fast medical fluid reaches the patient.

WO2024118733.headline: Two-chamber syringe for drug and flush
WO2024118733.summary: Giving a drug through a catheter usually means a second syringe to flush the line afterwards. This syringe has two chambers in line, one nested inside the plunger of the other, separated by a resealable valve, so a nurse can mix, deliver the dose and flush the catheter with a single instrument.

EP4568701.headline: Ferrying treatments across the blood-brain barrier
EP4568701.summary: Most drugs cannot pass from the bloodstream into the brain. These engineered proteins bind to the transferrin receptor, a doorway into the brain, and can carry attached molecules such as gene-silencing RNA across it, offering a route to treat neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson's and Alzheimer's.

US12074597.headline: Protecting chip connections from voltage surges
US12074597.summary: When several chips share a data bus, a connection can see a higher voltage than a chip is designed for, especially while powering up. This circuit senses whether the chip's own supply is above or below a safe midpoint and sets a protective reference voltage accordingly, preventing damage to the input and output transistors.

WO2024097595.headline: Syringe that disables itself after one use
WO2024097595.summary: Reusing syringes spreads infection, so single-use designs that cannot be refilled are valuable. This syringe has a cup-shaped stopper on the end of the plunger that uses suction to disable the syringe after the dose is delivered, preventing it from being drawn up again.

US11977523.headline: Quicker matching of log data to extraction rules
US11977523.summary: Software that analyses machine logs must test each incoming record against many rules to pull out useful fields, which is slow. This approach first checks whether a rule's fixed text snippets appear in the record and only then checks the full field pattern, so most rules are rejected cheaply and extraction runs faster.

WO2024112762.headline: Needle cap with built-in disinfectant
WO2024112762.summary: Before an injection, the needle or injection site is usually wiped with a separate alcohol swab. This needle shield includes a pre-cut foam pad soaked in disinfectant and glued inside the cover, so disinfection is built into the cap itself.

US12377995.headline: Hydrogen fuel cell propulsion in an aircraft tail
US12377995.summary: Electrifying aircraft requires fitting fuel cells, hydrogen tanks and motors without disrupting the airframe. This design places hydrogen tanks and fuel cells inside the tail section and mounts a propeller pod with an electric motor on each side of the tail, along with the cooling systems the fuel cells need.

US12026626.headline: Combining AI models to label online content
US12026626.summary: Online platforms need to tag text, images and other content with many labels at several levels of detail. This approach uses a mixture of neural networks, each trained on a different type of input, and combines their outputs to automatically generate appropriate labels for a given piece of content.

US12169983.headline: Picking the best face photo automatically
US12169983.summary: Streaming services show a headshot for each actor, but choosing a good one from thousands of frames is laborious. This system extracts faces from images, ranks them using rules about facial features, uses the ranking to train a model that scores face quality, and stores the best shots for display alongside a film or show.

US12175622.headline: Speeding up image distortion correction
US12175622.summary: Correcting lens distortion or reshaping an image requires fetching scattered pixels from the original, which is slow when memory is accessed randomly. This technique splits both images into blocks and overlapping regions, then sorts the processing order by region, row and column so the needed pixels are fetched in an orderly, cache-friendly sequence.

US12204873.headline: Merging two datasets without duplicates
US12204873.summary: Combining a new dataset with an existing one often creates duplicate or mismatched records. This method groups fields by data type, builds similarity scores and matrices, uses optimisation to find the best mapping between records, validates the matches, and then merges the data while applying the user's preferences on how conflicts are handled.

US12206800.headline: Security scans triggered by what changes
US12206800.summary: Scanning every computer on a network for vulnerabilities on a fixed schedule wastes resources and misses recent changes. Here a lightweight assistant on each machine reports events to a central scan engine, which responds by requesting a scan only when something has changed and when network capacity or the machine's schedule allows.

US12211275.headline: Faster highlighting of players in replays
US12211275.summary: Sports broadcasters want to draw a spotlight on a particular player in a replay almost instantly. This technique runs two jobs at once: one tracks every person in the clip with bounding boxes while an annotator marks the player of interest in a few frames; combining the two produces a highlight that follows the player through the replay.

US12217770.headline: Spotlighting the player with the ball
US12217770.summary: Viewers of sports video can lose track of who has the ball. This system detects players in each frame, works out which ones are on the pitch, identifies the one in possession and draws a visual spotlight on them, sized in proportion to the player's height on screen.

US12223659.headline: Reading road banking from 3D road models
US12223659.summary: Roads are banked on curves, and engineers need to extract this superelevation from 3D models. This tool takes cross-section slices along the road's alignment, finds the top surface edges in each, compares the cross-slopes of consecutive slices to detect banked stretches, and displays the results.

US12229994.headline: Robotic test rig for depth cameras
US12229994.summary: Depth-sensing cameras used in robots and warehouses need their accuracy verified. This set-up fixes reference boards with known 3D shapes, textures, steps and gaps to a robotic arm, which presents them to the camera from many angles; the captured data is compared with the known geometry to score accuracy, precision and coverage.

US12237026.headline: Denser read-only memory for chips
US12237026.summary: Read-only memory stores fixed data on a chip, and shrinking it saves space and power. This circuit design selects a column, passes the stored bit to a transistor linking two stages of local wiring, and reads the inverted value from the second stage, allowing a more compact memory cell arrangement.

US12242572.headline: Combining cheap and precise measurements in AI models
US12242572.summary: Accurate measurements of a physical system are expensive, while rough ones are cheap and plentiful. This method trains one model on the rough data, feeds its predictions as extra input to a second model trained on the scarce precise data, and fuses the two into a compact model that can run in real time.

US12255773.headline: Unlocking software features by tier and role
US12255773.summary: Software vendors sell applications in tiers and need to switch features on or off as a customer's subscription changes. This monitoring system watches each application instance's configuration, works out when its feature level should change, and reconfigures the user interface to show the features appropriate to the new level and the user's role.

US12271878.headline: Personalised in-app content from templates
US12271878.summary: Applications want to show messages tailored to each user without hand-writing every variant. When a user's device requests content, the system picks a template, evaluates rules against the user's context to fill in variable values, and returns personalised content built from the template.

WO2014122451.headline: Locking wallet records to the phone's chip
WO2014122451.summary: Mobile wallets store transaction histories that should not be readable if copied to another device. This method stores the history alongside the unique identifier of the phone's secure chip, and the wallet only allows access when the chip's identifier matches the stored one.

EP3017026.headline: Making more ethylene from crude oil
EP3017026.summary: Covers a process and plant for converting crude oil directly into petrochemicals with a higher yield of ethylene, the key building block for plastics. No abstract is available, so further detail cannot be given.

EP3017024.headline: Turning refinery leftovers into petrochemicals
EP3017024.summary: Heavy residues left after refining crude oil have little value. This process distils the feed, cracks the heavy bottom fraction with hydrogen, then splits the products into single-ring and multi-ring aromatic streams; the former goes to a gasoline hydrocracker and the latter to a ring-opening unit to make petrochemical feedstocks.

US8830766.headline: Faster, more reliable memory read circuits
US8830766.summary: Reading data from memory chips relies on sense amplifiers that must be reset quickly and work reliably despite variations in manufacturing, voltage and temperature. This self-timed circuit detects when a read has completed and resets the amplifier immediately, removing the safety margins that normally slow down memory access.

EP3385893.headline: Controlling robots in automated warehouses
EP3385893.summary: Automated warehouses use fleets of robots to move goods between storage and workstations. This covers methods and software for controlling the movement of those transporting devices and coordinating the fully or partly automated handling of goods at the workstations.

WO2014123593.headline: Cockpit lighting that signals aircraft status
WO2014123593.summary: Pilots must monitor many instruments to keep track of the aircraft's condition. This system has a processor identify the aircraft's status and adjust the cockpit lighting in response, so changes in light provide an at-a-glance indication of status.

EP3021947.headline: New compounds against tuberculosis
EP3021947.summary: Tuberculosis is increasingly resistant to existing antibiotics. These azaindole compounds block DprE1, an enzyme the bacterium needs to build its cell wall, and are proposed for treating tuberculosis and other mycobacterial infections.

EP2996338.headline: Sharper video prediction for next-generation compression
EP2996338.summary: Video compression works by predicting each frame from earlier ones. This covers techniques for generating higher-resolution predictions, adapted to the content, to improve coding efficiency in next-generation video formats.

EP2956006.headline: Purified gut bacteria to restore a healthy microbiome
EP2956006.summary: Antibiotics and illness can wipe out the beneficial bacteria in the gut. This treatment takes donor faecal material, purifies out the hardy spore-forming bacteria, and administers them so they take root and restore a healthy microbial balance, as an alternative to raw stool transplants.

US9178422.headline: More efficient voltage converter using one coil
US9178422.summary: Electronic devices need to convert one DC voltage to another with minimal energy loss. This converter uses a single inductor and a capacitor working in resonance, with three switches that steer current through three phases, to produce the output voltage efficiently.

WO2014130327.headline: Adjustable signal driver for chip connections
WO2014130327.summary: Chips send signals over connections whose electrical characteristics vary. This driver circuit can be configured to adjust its termination resistance, the voltage swing of its signals and how it shapes them, so one design can suit different channels.

EP2840800.headline: Adjusting volume by recognising the TV channel
EP2840800.summary: Sound levels vary between channels and programme types, forcing viewers to keep reaching for the remote. This system analyses the video picture to recognise which channel is showing, works out what kind of content is on, and adjusts the audio automatically.

WO2014138126.headline: Buy-and-sell suggestions from what you own
WO2014138126.summary: Online marketplaces know what shoppers browse but not what they already own. This system keeps an inventory of a user's possessions and assets, uses it to recommend items to buy or sell and communities to join, and shows the current market value of individual items or the whole collection.

EP2973004.headline: Upload a spreadsheet, ask it to predict
EP2973004.summary: Businesses hold tabular data but lack the expertise to build predictive models. This service takes an uploaded table, computes indices capturing the probabilistic relationships between rows and columns, stores them and exposes an interface through which users can ask predictive questions and receive answers.

US9291800.headline: Compact high-quality camera lens design
US9291800.summary: Camera lenses must balance sharpness, size and cost. This lens arrangement uses a front group of two negative meniscus lenses, one with an aspheric surface, plus a positive lens, followed by an aperture and a rear group, with glass properties chosen to control aberrations.

EP2981939.headline: Paying by alias from a mobile phone
EP2981939.summary: Paying in person or online typically requires sharing card details. Here a shopper gives a merchant only an alias; the server then asks the shopper's phone for a credential kept in its secure memory and combines it with one held on the server to obtain the payment credentials needed to complete the transaction.

EP3879892.headline: Connecting phones to two base stations at once
EP3879892.summary: Mobile networks can boost speeds by letting a phone use two base stations simultaneously. This procedure sets out how a phone connects to the second station, including exchanging access messages and receiving a separate temporary identifier from each station, and how connection failures are handled.

EP3061030.headline: Blocking malicious apps before they reach the network
EP3061030.summary: Malware on a computer often reveals itself when it tries to connect to the network. Here an agent intercepts such attempts and sends a fingerprint of the application and its local reputation score to a server, which looks up threat intelligence and tells the computer whether to allow or block it, also checking any libraries the program loaded.

US9478292.headline: Preparing memory cells ahead of read requests
US9478292.summary: Flash memory can be slow to respond when a read request arrives. This method checks whether storage cells meet a predefined condition and, if so, prepares them for use in advance, so later read requests from applications are served faster.

EP3346740.headline: Letting phones find each other directly on 4G
EP3346740.summary: Phones nearby could communicate directly without routing through the network, but they first need to discover one another. This scheme divides the radio resources set aside for discovery into sub-pools and has a phone send its discovery signal repeatedly using resources from different sub-pools, improving the chance of being found.

EP3068040.headline: Detecting motor faults from current signals
EP3068040.summary: Industrial induction motors can develop faults in their rotor or stator that lead to costly failures. This method measures the three-phase currents feeding the motor, combines them into a single signal, and compares its frequency spectrum against that of a healthy motor to spot developing faults without stopping the machine.

JP6191820.headline: Camera lens for smartphones
JP6191820.summary: Covers an imaging lens and the camera and portable device built around it. No abstract is available, so further detail cannot be given.

EP4016666.headline: Dry-made electrodes for lithium batteries
EP4016666.summary: Battery electrodes are usually made with solvents that must be dried off, adding cost and emissions. This electrode uses a dry binder combining PTFE with PVDF or polyethylene oxide in roughly equal parts, suitable for lithium-ion batteries and capacitors.

EP2945080.headline: Merging spreadsheets with matching suggestions
EP2945080.summary: Combining several spreadsheets by hand means finding which columns correspond. This tool profiles the selected spreadsheets, identifies matching columns and scores how well they match, previews the combined sheet with matches and gaps highlighted, and records the steps as a reusable template for other spreadsheets.

EP3134997.headline: Backup takeover for live video multicast
EP3134997.summary: Live video delivered to many viewers at once depends on a controller that can fail. This arrangement has a standby controller learn which video streams the primary is handling and, on detecting that the primary has failed, subscribe to those streams itself so viewing continues.

KR20150078689.headline: Better copper coating for circuit boards
KR20150078689.summary: When tiny holes in circuit boards are filled with copper, gaps and seams can form that make the board unreliable. This plating solution contains an additive that makes copper build up smoothly from the bottom of each hole, avoiding such defects and producing more dependable electronics.

EP3215900.headline: Teaching software robots by watching screens
EP3215900.summary: Many office tasks involve repetitive clicking and typing on a computer. This approach records screenshots while a person does the job, uses image recognition to work out each step, and turns them into instructions a software robot can follow automatically, removing the need for manual programming.

WO2013171729.headline: New drug compounds targeting immune regulation
WO2013171729.summary: A family of chemical compounds designed to act on a protein involved in regulating the immune system, with potential use in treating related diseases. Little further detail is available.

EP2765466.headline: Managing who can do what at power plants
EP2765466.summary: Large power plants run many local computer systems, and controlling staff access to each is cumbersome. Here a central server assigns roles to each user and passes the relevant permissions to local servers, so staff can be checked and allowed to perform only the tasks their role permits.

WO2014126920.headline: Cleaning sulphur from diesel exhaust filters
WO2014126920.summary: Diesel exhaust treatment systems gradually clog with sulphur, which reduces their ability to cut harmful emissions. This method estimates how much sulphur has built up and, when it passes a threshold, temporarily adjusts the engine so that the exhaust burns the sulphur off and restores performance.

EP3080640.headline: Shaping radio signals to fit two constraints
EP3080640.summary: Some radio and radar applications need a signal with a steady power level over time while also having a prescribed frequency profile. This step-by-step calculation alternates between the two requirements, refining a guess until a signal satisfying both closely enough is found, starting from a clever initial estimate.

WO2014107197.headline: Smarter touch handling and screen edge displays
WO2014107197.summary: Touchscreens waste effort processing touches on parts of the screen that are not in use. This design has the touch controller filter out touches in secondary regions before passing them on, and lets the device decide when to show content on the screen's edge based on sensors, content and user preferences.

WO2014169265.headline: Storing linked data in simple databases
WO2014169265.summary: Graph data, which records how things relate to one another, is normally kept in specialised databases. This technique encodes each relationship as a compact key so it can be stored and searched in a simple, fast key-value store, letting ordinary database systems answer questions about connected data.

EP3060213.headline: Combination antibiotic for resistant infections
EP3060213.summary: Bacteria increasingly resist existing antibiotics. This medicine combines the established antibiotic cefepime with a second compound, intended to improve treatment of bacterial infections.

EP3866558.headline: Reconnecting wireless devices automatically after dropouts
EP3866558.summary: When a wireless link between two gadgets, such as a phone and headphones, is lost, reconnecting can be slow or need user action. Here the device scans using a second wireless protocol to pick up the other device's address and restores the connection automatically.

EP3097104.headline: New compounds for fighting bacterial infections
EP3097104.summary: A group of nitrogen-containing chemical compounds, with methods for making them, intended for preventing or treating bacterial infections. Few further details are given.

WO2015040624.headline: Measuring network speed with timestamped test packets
WO2015040624.summary: Operators need to know how quickly data crosses their networks. A test packet is stamped with the time at one device and again at another, then sent to a central controller that uses the two stamps to calculate delays and other performance figures for the network.

EP2940296.headline: Reducing wind-shadow losses across wind farms
EP2940296.summary: Wind turbines slow the air behind them, so downwind turbines in a farm produce less power. This method tracks which turbines are affecting each other as conditions change, builds a predictive model of these wake effects from current and past data, and adjusts turbine settings to raise the farm's overall output.

EP2963866.headline: Routing traffic through services between networks
EP2963866.summary: Operators often want data passing between two networks to go through a service such as a firewall first. This controller takes a route learned from one network, rewrites it so the service point becomes the next stop, and shares it with the other network, so traffic is steered through the service automatically.

EP3043479.headline: Cheaper multi-channel signal conversion chips
EP3043479.summary: Electronics that read many sensor inputs at once need a converter for each channel, which takes space and power. This design gives each channel a small first-stage converter and shares a single second-stage converter and amplifier among them, cutting cost and size while keeping accuracy.

EP2943532.headline: Additive tablets for processing plastics
EP2943532.summary: Plastics makers add ingredients to change a material's properties during melting and moulding. This is a compact tablet combining such an additive with a processing aid that softens at or below the melting temperature, making the additives easier to handle and blend into the plastic.

EP3041296.headline: Sharing internet connections between nearby devices
EP3041296.summary: A device with internet access advertises what connections it has available and their characteristics. Nearby devices send connection requests with their needs, and the first device picks a suitable connection and shares it, letting devices find and use the best available network around them.

EP3198297.headline: Splitting radar processing across several chips
EP3198297.summary: Car radar systems need to process large amounts of signal data quickly to detect objects. Here several radar chips each do the first part of the processing on their own channels, then pass partial results to a central unit that completes the detection, allowing bigger systems with more antennas.

EP3182288.headline: Predicting how long big data queries take
EP3182288.summary: Companies running database queries on large computing clusters struggle to predict how long jobs will take. This approach runs small test jobs on a small cluster, measures how each stage behaves, and builds a statistical model that forecasts execution time for the same kind of queries on much larger clusters and datasets.

WO2016061093.headline: Paying by phone without an internet connection
WO2016061093.summary: Mobile payments usually fail when there is no network signal. This system stores encrypted payment data on the phone, uses a built-in risk check to decide whether an offline payment can be approved, holds completed payments in a queue, and sends them to the payment provider once a connection returns.

WO2017135977.headline: Spam filter that keeps learning from mistakes
WO2017135977.summary: Spam filters make errors, and finding them to improve the system is laborious. Here each item labelled as spam gets a confidence score; items whose label conflicts with what is known about their sender are flagged as possible errors and sent for review, while confident spam is filtered, so the model improves continuously.

US10048744.headline: Chips that cooperate to stay cool
US10048744.summary: When several chips sit in one package, one chip overheating can be eased by having another use less power. This design adds a direct signal line between chips so that a chip exceeding its temperature limit can tell its neighbour to cut power consumption, keeping the whole package within safe limits.

WO2017211393.headline: Improved spray nozzles for dishwashers
WO2017211393.summary: A dishwasher spray arm with one or more nozzles for directing heated washing liquid into the tub, used together with a heater and a control unit offering different washing modes. The abstract gives little detail on the specific improvement.

EP3254305.headline: 3D-printed parts for chip-making chambers
EP3254305.summary: Components inside semiconductor processing chambers suffer from film build-up and high temperatures. This part is made as a single solid piece with a deliberately textured surface of raised features, which is designed to reduce stress in deposited films and allow cooler operation.

US10037504.headline: Spotting wasted effort on factory floors
US10037504.summary: Manufacturers want to find where time is wasted in production. This system analyses video of a work area, tracks people and objects across frames, identifies their interactions, and encodes the sequence of subtasks. It then classifies which subtasks are wasteful and calculates how long they take, helping managers improve productivity.

EP3247072.headline: Keeping data flowing when a network exit fails
EP3247072.summary: In certain business networks, traffic to a customer site normally passes through one designated exit device, and its failure interrupts service. Here an upstream device relabels the traffic so a backup device can deliver it instead, keeping broadcast and group traffic flowing while the fault is repaired.

US9845164.headline: Robot vehicles patrolling industrial plants
US9845164.summary: Checking equipment across a large industrial plant is slow and risky for staff. This system sends an autonomous vehicle fitted with sensors along stored routes, transmits the readings to a central plant information system, and compares them with historical data to detect events such as faults or leaks.

WO2016156894.headline: Styled front light arrangement for motorcycles
WO2016156894.summary: A motorcycle front cover design in which a small position light sits in a raised section at the top centre, below the headlight and above the indicators, surrounded by a recess that widens towards the rear. The arrangement is mainly about the shape and placement of the light and bodywork.

EP3297747.headline: Lower-energy way to capture carbon dioxide
EP3297747.summary: Capturing carbon dioxide from industrial exhaust usually needs a lot of energy to regenerate the capture material. This process uses a solid absorbent coated with potassium carbonate and only partly regenerates it with a low-carbon-dioxide gas stream before reusing it, cutting the overall energy required.

EP3322448.headline: Combining a tumour drug with immunotherapy
EP3322448.summary: Immune checkpoint inhibitors help the body's immune system attack cancer but do not work for everyone. This treatment pairs them with Talabostat, a drug that blocks certain enzymes in and around tumours, aiming to improve the immune response and slow tumour growth.

WO2017015078.headline: Collecting sales tax automatically at payment
WO2017015078.summary: Governments lose revenue when indirect taxes such as VAT are not passed on by sellers. This system works out whether tax is due on a card transaction, calculates the amount, deducts it when the payment is settled, and forwards it straight to the tax authority, bypassing the merchant.

EP3350858.headline: Automatic health checks for fuel cell stacks
EP3350858.summary: Fuel cells degrade in ways that are hard to see from the outside. This system runs an electrical test on many fuel cells at once without human involvement, extracts two indicators of internal condition from the results, and triggers corrective action when either indicator crosses a warning threshold.

WO2017075578.headline: Smarter coasting to save vehicle fuel
WO2017075578.summary: Vehicles can save fuel by disconnecting the engine and coasting, but must re-engage it before speed drifts too far. This system compares actual and predicted speed with thresholds to decide whether to keep coasting or reconnect the engine, allowing brief speed excursions when they are expected to correct themselves.

WO2017179003.headline: Antibiotic drops for eye and ear infections
WO2017179003.summary: Topical formulations of a class of powerful antibiotics known as lipoglycopeptides, optionally combined with anti-inflammatory drugs, for treating infections and related conditions of the eye and ear.

EP3396855.headline: Solar tracker that needs no external power
EP3396855.summary: Devices that follow the sun usually require motors and power. Here light-sensing cells generate small currents that feed electromagnets, which pull a movable weight towards the brightest side. The shifting weight tilts the sensor array towards or away from the light, so it tracks a moving light source entirely on its own.

WO2017099734.headline: Reminding drivers of phones left in cars
WO2017099734.summary: People often leave their phones behind in parked cars. The car pairs with the phone and periodically tells it where it is; when the car is switched off, it sends a final location along with a shutdown flag, which the phone can use to warn its owner before they walk away.

EP3251947.headline: Automatic aborted take-off at low speeds
EP3251947.summary: If an engine fails during take-off below a certain speed, the aircraft must stop safely on the runway. This system detects such a failure automatically and carries out the abort sequence itself, reducing stopping distance. That allows heavier loads, longer range or use of shorter runways.

EP3629872.headline: Rotating spray arm for cleaner dishes
EP3629872.summary: A dishwasher spray device with a rotating hub carrying nozzles that spray cleaning liquid into the tub, intended to improve cleaning performance. The abstract gives little further detail.

US10104621.headline: Wi-Fi receiver that saves power listening
US10104621.summary: Wireless devices waste energy keeping their full receiver on while waiting for data. This design runs only half of the receive circuitry to check whether an incoming signal actually contains a data packet, and switches on the rest only when one is detected, extending battery life.

WO2017108053.headline: Safer lifting of giant wind turbine blades
WO2017108053.summary: Wind turbine blades are enormous and awkward to move with cranes. This lifting rig holds a blade in a cradle hung from a yoke that can slide along the cradle, so the blade's tilt can be adjusted conveniently and safely while suspended, making it easier to manoeuvre between sites.

EP3494194.headline: Turning woody waste into liquid fuel
EP3494194.summary: Converting plant biomass into fuel is hampered by chlorides in the raw material. This process mixes in a chloride-trapping material, compresses the blend into pellets, and heats it with hydrogen and a catalyst under pressure, producing a liquid hydrocarbon product while removing char and spent catalyst.

EP3457240.headline: Live wiring maps for factory equipment
EP3457240.summary: Keeping wiring diagrams of a plant accurate is tedious and error-prone. This system uses real-time data from sensors on installed devices and a lookup table to work out how they are physically connected, draws the wiring diagram automatically and overlays live connection status so engineers see faults at a glance.

EP3379434.headline: Designing stronger parts for 3D printing
EP3379434.summary: 3D-printed parts behave differently depending on the direction they are printed, which conventional design tools ignore. This method repeatedly simulates loads and constraints while accounting for those direction-dependent material properties, arriving at the lightest shape that still meets safety margins, together with the best printing orientation.

US10505655.headline: Coordinating flexible Ethernet links across networks
US10505655.summary: Telecom networks increasingly bundle several Ethernet connections into flexible groups. This method extends a standard network signalling protocol so that network nodes can tell each other which group and which physical links to use, and configure the bundled connection automatically.

WO2018141914.headline: Washer-dryer with mini wash inside door
WO2018141914.summary: Small or delicate items are easily damaged or lost in a full drum. This washer-dryer has a door whose curved inner window bulges into the drum, creating a separate small washing chamber between the two door panes where delicate laundry can be washed on its own.

US11082754.headline: Cameras that anticipate the action at events
US11082754.summary: Multi-camera broadcasts of sport or events can miss key moments. This system combines live video feeds, sensors worn by participants and historical performance data to predict where the next notable action will happen, steers cameras to focus there, and broadcasts multiple views of the resulting multi-dimensional video to viewers.

EP3367137.headline: Sharing severe weather alerts between aircraft
EP3367137.summary: Pilots need timely warnings of dangerous weather. Here aircraft detect severe weather with onboard sensors using thresholds tuned to what other aircraft need, report it with time and location to a ground station, which merges it with other data, forecasts its movement over a grid, and uplinks warnings to aircraft heading that way.

EP3523727.headline: Building processors from several connected chips
EP3523727.summary: Rather than making one large processor chip, which is costly and prone to defects, this approach builds a processor from several physically separate smaller chips joined by an electrical interconnect. The abstract gives little further detail.

EP3447717.headline: Simulating composite materials to cut testing
EP3447717.summary: Working out the properties of composite materials normally requires expensive, slow physical testing. This method models the material at several scales, from microscopic ingredients up to the whole structure, passing results from each level to the next, so engineers can predict how a structure will behave and fine-tune designs with less testing.

US10205440.headline: Memory cells that remember during sleep mode
US10205440.summary: Chips save power by switching off their clock in sleep mode, but risk losing stored data. These circuit designs add a control unit and holding latch that keep the last data value safe while the clock is off, then hand it back when normal operation resumes, enabling very low-power standby.

EP3562486.headline: Under-the-tongue drug to calm agitation
EP3562486.summary: Agitation in people with dementia or psychiatric conditions is often treated with heavy sedatives. This method gives the drug dexmedetomidine under the tongue at a dose that calms the patient without causing significant sedation, offering a gentler way to manage agitation episodes.

CN108622278.headline: Wind-cooled battery mount for scooters
CN108622278.summary: Batteries on electric and hybrid scooters can overheat. This mounting fixes the battery under the front end of the seat, in a box with ventilated lid, so that airflow while riding cools it naturally.

EP3707023.headline: Powering truck equipment with engine off
EP3707023.summary: Vehicles such as refrigerated lorries need power for auxiliary equipment even when parked. This system adds a motor-generator and battery connected via a power take-off, so the equipment can run from the engine while driving and from the electric motor when the engine is off, with gearing chosen for each mode.

EP3653854.headline: Checking diesel soot filters without removal
EP3653854.summary: Diesel particulate filters must be monitored to ensure they still trap soot. This method logs exhaust temperature and pressure data, estimates the filter's condition using a statistical procedure when conditions are right, and after enough data points uses a machine-learning classifier to judge whether the filter is healthy or failing.

US10917587.headline: Turn a photo of text into charts
US10917587.summary: Typing data from printed documents into software is slow. This method photographs an object containing text, recognises the characters, organises them into structured data, and generates a graphical image such as a chart that is displayed directly on the user's device screen.

EP3864513.headline: Sharing work between overloaded smart sensors
EP3864513.summary: In networks of connected sensors, one node can become overloaded with pending tasks while others sit idle. This method spots when a node's backlog exceeds its available resources, identifies tasks another node could handle, and hands them over so the network keeps running smoothly.

EP3530718.headline: Turning crude oil straight into chemicals
EP3530718.summary: Refineries normally produce fuels, with chemicals as a sideline. This process integrates several refining steps, including coking, intensive catalytic cracking and naphtha cracking, with recovery units and a gasifier, so that nearly all of the crude oil is converted into high-value chemicals such as light olefins and aromatics.

EP3880506.headline: Electric cars charging each other in convoys
EP3880506.summary: Electric vehicles fitted with wireless power transfer units at front and rear can link up into a chain. Each vehicle can act as a power source, a receiver or a relay passing power along the line, letting vehicles share charge between them, for instance while travelling together.

WO2019005105.headline: Faster memory access through early warnings
WO2019005105.summary: When a processor needs data not held in its fast cache, waiting for main memory slows everything down. Here the processor sends a quick advance notice over a fast path so the memory controller can start waking the right memory bank before the full request arrives via the slower path, trimming delays.

EP3536764.headline: Cleaner diesel with less sulphur
EP3536764.summary: Regulations demand diesel with very little sulphur and good combustion quality. This refinery process arranges hydrotreating stages in a mix of co-current and counter-current configurations to remove sulphur more thoroughly, yielding diesel with under ten parts per million sulphur and a high cetane rating.

EP3939384.headline: Induction hob that protects itself from overheating
EP3939384.summary: Induction hobs can overheat their coils and electronics during heavy use. This design mounts the coil on a support that moves it further from the cooking surface as the coil or its drive circuit gets hotter, reducing heat transfer and protecting the components without interrupting cooking.

US10951639.headline: Two-stage fault detection for industrial plants
US10951639.summary: Industrial control systems need to catch abnormal behaviour quickly. This method runs a first detector at the plant's network gateway using one set of sensor data; if it flags something, a second, different detector in the cloud checks another set of data. An alert is raised when either detects an anomaly.

WO2019089791.headline: Precise adjustable clock signals for chips
WO2019089791.summary: Electronic chips often need clock frequencies that are not simple fractions of a reference. This circuit uses an analogue interpolator with digitally controlled delay, a comparator and a divider, steered by a digital control section, to produce a clean output clock at a precisely adjustable fractional rate with little jitter.

EP3791284.headline: Resolving conflicts in globally replicated databases
EP3791284.summary: When several servers around the world can each update the same database, they may write conflicting versions of a record. This system lets each kind of data be assigned its own rule for settling conflicts, such as last writer wins, custom logic or manual review, and applies the appropriate rule automatically.

EP3899251.headline: Balancing wind turbine output against wear
EP3899251.summary: Wind farm controllers must decide how much power each turbine should produce. This method ranks turbines by both their current output and how much fatigue they have accumulated, then sets power targets accordingly, so the farm meets demand while spreading wear and extending turbine life.

EP3889278.headline: Low-carbon pellets from iron ore dust
EP3889278.summary: Fine iron ore particles are hard to use in furnaces without energy-intensive heat treatment. This process binds the fines with sodium silicate, nanomaterials, catalysts and other additives, shapes them into pellets or briquettes and cures them at room temperature, producing a robust, water-resistant feed without emitting carbon dioxide or other harmful gases.

US10746123.headline: Self-learning control for engine air and fuel
US10746123.summary: Engine air and fuel systems are usually tuned by hand. Here a software agent learns, by trial and reward, a policy that reads the engine's current state from sensors and sets targets for air handling and fuelling, continually updating itself so the engine runs more efficiently under changing conditions.

EP4103114.headline: Flexible cooling pad with adjustable air cushion
EP4103114.summary: A cooling system made of many linked cells carrying coolant, covered by a flexible sheet with an air gap in between. An air pump changes the size of that gap, allowing the degree of contact and cooling to be adjusted.

EP4097546.headline: Detecting unauthorised tampering with wind farms
EP4097546.summary: Wind farms are vulnerable to cyber intrusion. This method uses a trained model, fed with environmental, operational and maintenance scheduling data, to predict how the farm should be operating. If actual commands from users deviate significantly from that prediction, the system flags a likely unauthorised access.

EP3974968.headline: Faster AI maths on graphics chips
EP3974968.summary: Machine-learning workloads rely on vast numbers of multiply-and-add calculations. This graphics processor includes a core that handles a single instruction to multiply two numbers in a compact 16-bit floating-point format and add a third, speeding up AI computations while using less memory.

EP3976419.headline: Blockchain records for electric vehicle charging
EP3976419.summary: Charging an electric car at points run by different energy suppliers raises billing and trust issues. Here a central operator verifies the vehicle and charging point, authorises the charge, and records the transaction on a blockchain for that supplier, with all suppliers' records also kept in a master blockchain.

WO2020183496.headline: Cheaper catalyst for cleaner motorcycle exhaust
WO2020183496.summary: Motorcycles must meet tightening emission limits. This catalyst system converts harmful hydrocarbons, carbon monoxide and nitrogen oxides in exhaust into less harmful gases, while using precious metals sparingly to cut cost and keeping back pressure low so engine performance is not harmed.

EP3942662.headline: Smarter power switching for electric vehicles
EP3942662.summary: Electric and hybrid vehicles must juggle a high-voltage battery, low-voltage systems and external power sources. This power electronics assembly uses a controller that works out the vehicle's operating mode and sets switches to connect the right components to the main battery, with an efficient inverter and built-in circuit protection.

EP3989452.headline: Choosing Wi-Fi access point teams wisely
EP3989452.summary: Modern Wi-Fi lets several access points serve one device together, but this only works if the links between them are good enough. This control method checks whether candidate groups of access points have backhaul connections meeting the requirements for coordinated and multi-link operation before selecting a group to serve the device.

US11949703.headline: Finding the root cause of IT problems
US11949703.summary: Monitoring systems for computing infrastructure track many metrics, each throwing up its own alarms. This method detects anomalies in each time series, assigns each a time window, and groups metrics whose anomalies overlap in time. The resulting clusters help pinpoint and automatically fix the underlying cause.

WO2021021533.headline: Predicting chip inspection images from designs
WO2021021533.summary: Inspecting semiconductor wafers with electron microscopes is slow. This system trains a deep-learning model on pairs of real microscope images and matching 3D design data, then generates simulated images directly from new designs, allowing defects and imaging conditions to be predicted before physical inspection.

EP4100633.headline: Keeping exhaust hot when cylinders switch off
EP4100633.summary: Engines save fuel by shutting down some cylinders, but this can cool the exhaust so much that emission-control systems stop working properly. This method selects from several measures, such as bypassing coolers or adjusting the turbocharger and injection timing, to keep exhaust temperatures up during cylinder deactivation.

WO2021055027.headline: Correcting distorted camera images efficiently
WO2021055027.summary: Wide-angle lenses distort images, and straightening them in real time demands a lot of memory bandwidth. This circuit works through pre-computed correction maps in sequence, loading only the blocks of pixels needed for each output tile and writing the corrected tiles out, producing an undistorted image efficiently.

US10986118.headline: Blocking malicious links opened by apps
US10986118.summary: Mobile apps can be tricked into opening web links that attack the phone's browser. This method intercepts messages an app sends, extracts any web address, checks its reputation, and if the site is known to be malicious takes protective action before the browser is exposed.

US11030782.headline: Realistic virtual try-on of clothes online
US11030782.summary: Online shoppers cannot see how garments would look on a given body. This system uses neural networks to warp a product photo to fit a model image in stages, works out exactly which parts of the model to replace, and blends them into a convincing virtual try-on picture.

EP3958161.headline: Smarter laptop lid with its own processor
EP3958161.summary: Laptop lids house cameras, microphones and touchscreens whose data normally travels through the hinge to the main processor. Placing a dedicated controller in the lid processes that data locally, enabling wake-on-voice or face, smoother touch response, stronger privacy, fewer hinge wires and longer battery life.

US11159445.headline: Routing network data to multiple on-chip processors
US11159445.summary: A single chip may contain a network switch alongside several processing units. This design lets the switch decide which internal processor a data frame should go to and picks a dedicated memory channel to deliver it, so multiple on-chip endpoints can be served efficiently.

EP4158168.headline: Preventing condensation inside engine air intakes
EP4158168.summary: Cooled intake air in turbocharged engines can form water droplets that damage components. This control system monitors engine conditions and adjusts the coolant temperature entering the air cooler so that the air stays above its dew point, preventing condensation before the intake manifold.

EP4274449.headline: Fridge drawer with adjustable temperature zones
EP4274449.summary: Different foods keep best at different temperatures, but fridge drawers usually offer one setting. This drawer has pivoting dividers that split it into separate compartments, each with its own temperature sensor and ducted airflow from multiple fans, so each section can be held at a different temperature.

EP4203564.headline: Powering down idle servers at network edges
EP4203564.summary: Small computing clusters at the network edge waste energy if all machines stay on. This method schedules workloads onto a subset of machines and then adjusts the power state of each machine accordingly, switching idle ones down and bringing them back as demand changes.

EP4266764.headline: Cutting power use across many IoT devices
EP4266764.summary: Large fleets of connected sensors drain batteries quickly. This system gathers each device's operating settings, estimates a cost function for its power use, examines how transmissions and receptions change that cost, and then reconfigures devices with the settings that minimise consumption.

EP4130198.headline: Refining waste plastic oil into useful fuels
EP4130198.summary: Oil made by heating waste plastics is hard to upgrade. This process feeds it into a refinery's existing delayed coking unit alongside heavy residual oil, using a hot refinery stream to preheat the plastic feed, raising yields of liquid and gas products and lowering coke without new hardware.

EP4396679.headline: Shifting computing to where renewable power is
EP4396679.summary: Data centres powered by wind or solar face fluctuating supply. This system spreads workloads across clusters in different locations whose renewable energy patterns complement one another, so that the combined group always has enough power available to run the software reliably.

US11966787.headline: Giving priority to the apps you use
US11966787.summary: When a computer runs short of memory or processing power, important programs can stall. This approach ranks running processes dynamically, taking into account how actively the user engages with them, predicts which is about to be starved, and reallocates resources from lower-ranked processes to keep it responsive.

US11651535.headline: Dashboard for monitoring AI model health
US11651535.summary: Organisations using many predictive models need to know when they stop performing well. This system organises health measurements into a hierarchy of measures, categories and models, computes indicators of each model's performance, and displays them in an interactive visual interface for monitoring.

EP4374561.headline: Automatic set-up of network devices in cloud
EP4374561.summary: Connecting new network equipment to a cloud management platform usually means configuring each device by hand, which is slow and error-prone. This process distributes the required connection settings to devices automatically and links them to the correct customer account, whether they sit on-premises, in the cloud or both.

US11728535.headline: Cooling plates built into battery pack walls
US11728535.summary: Electric vehicle batteries must be kept cool. This battery module housing has an end wall made of two plastic plates with a slot between them for an electrical connector, and channels inside the plates carry coolant fed from a cooling plate, so the housing itself helps remove heat.

US11599399.headline: Keeping two business software systems in sync
US11599399.summary: Companies often need the same record to exist in two different software applications. This method detects a newly created object in one application, fetches its current state, creates a matching object in the second application, and stores the second system's identifier back in the first, keeping both linked.

EP4281926.headline: Rendering only the parts of video that change
EP4281926.summary: Redrawing every pixel of each video frame wastes processing power. This system works out which regions actually changed from one frame to the next, groups them into blocks aligned with the graphics chip's tile layout, builds a tree of regions and selects an efficient set to redraw, saving work on the display.

US11734159.headline: Picking which software tests matter most
US11734159.summary: Running every automated test after each code change is slow. This technique builds a map of which functions call which and which tests cover them, then uses it to rank the tests most relevant to a given change, so developers can run the most informative tests first.

WO2023180685.headline: Stopping fake connection floods earlier
WO2023180685.summary: Attackers overwhelm servers by starting many secure connections that are expensive to verify. Here the client includes a one-time password in its first message, derived from a shared secret; a gateway checks it immediately and drops connections that fail, before the costly certificate checks, blunting denial-of-service attacks.

US12339728.headline: Graphics chips that save power on memory
US12339728.summary: Graphics chips often run their memory at full speed regardless of need. This system monitors the workload being processed and dynamically adjusts the voltage and clock frequency of the memory subsystem to match it, saving energy when demand is lower.

US11709522.headline: Automatic slow-down for overheating accelerator cards
US11709522.summary: Programmable accelerator cards can draw unpredictable power depending on what users load onto them. This technique continuously monitors power and temperature and throttles the clock when limits are exceeded, so users can run the card harder on average while it protects itself automatically.

EP4539951.headline: AI-verified skills recorded as digital tokens
EP4539951.summary: Skills gained in online environments such as games or courses are hard to prove elsewhere. This system uses an AI model to assess a user's progress and proficiency, then assigns a value to a digital token with a non-transferable personal part and an exchangeable part that can be recognised across platforms.

US12008488.headline: Installing software components in the right order
US12008488.summary: Cloud applications are deployed as packages with many interdependent sub-components, and installing them out of order causes failures. This system reads a package's dependency list, builds a graph of what depends on what, and deploys the components in an order that respects those dependencies.

US12254313.headline: Finding the right documents and experts for code
US12254313.summary: Developers often lack context about why code was written. This tool analyses version history such as pull requests, extracts key phrases, and uses them to find and rank relevant documents and people, then surfaces that information directly within the developer's coding environment.

US11876521.headline: Fine-tuning signal timing on chips
US11876521.summary: Chips that exchange data at high speed need precise control over the timing of signals. This circuit delays a timing signal in coarse steps using two interleaved chains of logic gates, then refines the delay in fine steps, and allows the delay settings to be updated while running.

US11943138.headline: Catching duplicate router IDs on networks
US11943138.summary: If two routers are accidentally given the same identifier, routing can break in confusing ways. This method watches for incoming routing packets that meet certain conditions, counts them over a timed window, and when the count passes a threshold concludes that another device shares its identifier.
